title: Strain-enabled dynamical magnetoelectric coupling in BaFe$_{12}$O$_{19}$
summary: Optical excitation has emerged as a powerful tool for manipulating and creating non-equilibrium phases of matter. Yet, the pathways available for optical control are intrinsically limited by the symmetries and interactions of the equilibrium system. Here, we demonstrate that these pathways can be redesigned through atomic-structural engineering to access hidden dynamical properties. By combining resonant vibrational excitation with epitaxial strain, we realize a light-induced, room-temperature multiferroic state in strained thin films of the technologically relevant hexagonal ferrimagnet, barium hexaferrite (BaFe$_{12}$O$_{19}$, BaM). Time-resolved second harmonic generation and magneto-optical Kerr effect measurements reveal an enhanced ferroelectric polarization together with a weakening of the magnetic moment upon exciting mid-infrared phonons in strained BaM thin films, but not in the bulk material. Structural analysis and first-principles-based theory show that this effect is enabled by strain-generated displacement of Fe$^{3+}$ ions, which break the local symmetry and facilitate an emergent dynamical magnetoelectric coupling. Both the strong lattice excitation and strain-induced symmetry breaking are essential for enabling this dynamical coupling, promising an important template for designing otherwise inaccessible non-equilibrium phenomena.

title: Translation Method Bounds for 3D Isotropic Conductivity--Shear Modulus and the Search for Attaining Microstructures
summary: We compute conductivity--shear-modulus cross-property bounds in three-dimensional isotropic two-phase composites using the translation method, and obtain the tightest bounds reported to date. To assess attainability, we perform unit-cell topology optimization on thousands of distinct initial structures and compare optimized designs to the isotropic bounds using an effective-medium approximation that models the macroscopic material as an isotropic assembly of randomly oriented grains. The best jointly performing designs are consistently bicontinuous, triply periodic minimal surface-like microstructures; however, a small but notable gap to the translation bound remains.

title: Electrical Degradation of Vertical $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ Schottky Barrier Diodes Under Au-Ion Irradiation to a Fluence of $1.3 \times 10^7$ cm$^{-2}$
summary: The electrical degradation and time-dependent current behavior of vertical $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ Schottky barrier diodes (SBDs) subjected to energetic Au-ion irradiation were systematically investigated. Two successive irradiation exposures were conducted under a constant reverse bias of $-100$ V to evaluate the effects of heavy-ion irradiation on device performance and transient current response. Following irradiation, the devices exhibited degraded forward conduction, increased specific on-resistance, enhanced reverse leakage current, and reduced apparent carrier concentration. During irradiation, pronounced increases in leakage current and transient current spikes were observed. Following each beam termination, the leakage current exhibited an initial rapid decay followed by a slower relaxation process. Single-exponential fitting identified distinct fast and slow relaxation components, while a double-exponential model provided a more comprehensive description of the overall current decay. After the second irradiation exposure, the characteristic time constants of the fast and slow relaxation processes increased from 33.50 to 40.64 s and from 190.35 to 282.29 s, respectively, indicating prolonged recovery dynamics under repeated irradiation. A charge-trapping-based model is proposed to explain the irradiation-induced current enhancement and subsequent fast and slow relaxation processes through modulation and gradual recovery of the effective Schottky tunneling barrier. These findings provide insights into the relationship between heavy-ion-induced electrical degradation and time-dependent current relaxation in $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ SBDs.

title: Density-dependent photocarrier recombination in $γ$-InSe
summary: We studied the photocarrier dynamics in $γ$-InSe using femtosecond transient reflectance spectroscopy. By measuring the dependence of the differential reflectance on the injected carrier density, we established an empirical relation between the optical response and carrier density, allowing quantitative analysis of the recombination dynamics. The carrier decay exhibits a strong density dependence, indicating a substantial contribution from nonlinear recombination. At high carrier densities, the dynamics are dominated by a second-order recombination process, with a rate constant of $3.8\times10^{-6}~\mathrm{cm^3\,s^{-1}}$. At low densities, the decay becomes approximately exponential, with a carrier lifetime of about 7 ps. We also resolved an initial rise of the band-edge response with a time constant of less than 1 ps, which is attributed to hot-carrier cooling. These results reveal the competition between first-order and second-order recombination in $γ$-InSe and provide quantitative insights into its ultrafast photocarrier dynamics.

title: A colored look at anyons and parastatistics
comment: 20 pages; based on the plenary talk at the XLIII Workshop on Geometric Methods in Physics, Białystok, Poland, July 2026
summary: Color Lie (super)algebras were introduced in 1978 by Rittenberg and Wyler as generalizations of ordinary Lie (super)algebras. These color structures, graded by abelian groups, are defined by brackets which satisfy generalized Jacobi identities. Only recently the relevance of color Lie (super)algebras to physical applications has been pointed out and proved. The color framework not only describes, but also provides physical signatures for two broad types of parastatistics (particles beyond ordinary bosons/fermions): i) paraparticles which are exchanged via the permutation group and can exist in any space dimension D and ii) anyons (exchanged via the braid group), which exist up to D=2 space dimensions. This paper presents an update of the recent advancements which motivate a brand new "colored look" at questions involving parastatistics and braid statistics.

title: A Causal Schrödinger-Newton Theory that Conserves Energy and Momentum
summary: This paper provides a theoretical justification for using the Causal-Conditional Schrödinger-Newton theory (CCSN) as a phenomenological model for classical gravity sourced by quantum matter. In CCSN, the gravitational field is driven not by expectation values in the global quantum state, but by conditional expectation values of the stress-energy tensor evaluated on local states determined by measurement records in the causal past. Because these local states are defined operationally from measurement records, the formulation is independent of any particular interpretation of quantum measurement while leading to unambiguous phenomenological dynamics. We apply this framework to a self-gravitating optomechanical system under continuous measurement and show that the resulting stochastic Schrödinger evolution, augmented by a classical gravitational field sourced by local conditional stress-energy expectations, can be made consistent with energy-momentum conservation by introducing a corrector tensor. The corrector restores the conservation law without altering the leading Newtonian predictions of CCSN, contributing only negligible post-Newtonian corrections in current experimental regimes. These results place CCSN on firmer theoretical footing and clarify its role as a viable phenomenological model for ongoing and future tests of classical gravity coupled to quantum matter.

title: Tunable first-order transitions and magnetic hysteresis in Bernal pentalayer graphene
summary: In two-dimensional electron systems, strong Coulomb interactions can spontaneously lift flavor degeneracies such as spin and valley, producing first-order transitions with hysteretic switching of interest for memory devices. The subband degree of freedom in multiband systems may be viewed as a flavor that not only participates in such transitions but also enables control of the hysteretic behavior, as a displacement field can shift the energy difference between subbands. Here, we demonstrate this principle in Bernal-stacked pentalayer graphene, whose low-energy spectrum comprises a monolayer-like Dirac sub-band together with light and heavy bilayer-like sub-bands. Local compressibility measurements resolve a fully symmetry-broken Landau-level spectrum and a sequence of phase transitions that occur when Landau levels of different subbands cross, at which strong interactions redistribute the occupation among flavors. We show that these transitions exhibit hysteretic Hall responses in magnetic field, confirming their first-order character, and that the magnitude and sign of the hysteresis are tuned by the displacement field, as expected from the subband Landau-level ordering determined in compressibility measurements. Our work establishes the subband degree of freedom in multiband systems as a resource for engineering hysteretic switching, and highlights how local thermodynamic measurements can link microscopic insights to macroscopic responses in quantum materials.

title: Light-cone distributions of vector and scalar bound states in the Schwinger model from tensor networks
summary: Light-cone distributions encode the partonic structure of hadrons, but they involve real-time correlations that Euclidean lattice methods cannot access directly. We compute the parton distribution functions (PDFs) and light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) of the vector and scalar meson bound states of the massive Schwinger model with tensor networks. Using the Kogut-Susskind lattice Hamiltonian with the gauge field eliminated through Gauss's law, we prepare the vacuum and the mesons as matrix product states and identify the vector and scalar mesons through their charge conjugation and momentum. The gauge-invariant light-cone correlators that define both distributions are evaluated directly in Minkowski space by real-time evolution. The two mesons exhibit qualitatively different light-cone structure, dictated by charge conjugation. The vector meson has a single-peaked PDF and a symmetric LCDA, while the scalar meson has a double-peaked PDF and an antisymmetric LCDA, whose vanishing zeroth moment requires a normalization through its first moment. The decay constants obtained from local matrix elements and from the moments of the LCDAs agree, and approach predictions from nonrelativistic model as the fermion mass increases. For the relatively large masses considered in this work, the PDFs closely follow the squared LCDAs, showing that the mesons are dominated by their valence component. Our results demonstrate tensor networks as a practical route to light-cone distributions of ground-state as well as excited hadrons in low-dimensional gauge theories.

title: Exact nonstationary heat-excess statistics in the weakly asymmetric Kipnis--Marchioro--Presutti model
summary: Exact nonstationary large-deviation statistics remain scarce for interacting many-body systems. Here we employ the macroscopic fluctuation theory (MFT) to determine the complete long-time statistics of heat excess produced by an initially localized heat pulse in the weakly asymmetric Kipnis--Marchioro--Presutti model. We find a remarkable nonlocal canonical transformation which maps the weakly asymmetric MFT problem, including its initial and terminal conditions, onto the symmetric problem, previously solved exactly. The resulting rate function is an explicit nonlinear deformation of its symmetric counterpart. We also extend the solution to heat measured beyond an arbitrary observation point.

title: Locality from Nonlocality: Symmetry Relocalization and Gauging of Lattice Dirac Fermions
summary:
Spatially nonlocal symmetries need not imply nonlocal gauge dynamics. Nonlocal canonical transformations make certain exact nonlocal compact symmetries of free lattice Dirac fermions onsite while retaining sufficient Hamiltonian locality for gauging. Symmetry relocalization yields exact or emergent gauge locality in 1D, 2D, and 3D, subject to lattice structure, topology, and anomalies.
  In 1D, a Hamiltonian-preserving transformation exchanges onsite vector and nonlocal spectral axial charges of a half-filled chain, enabling local gauging of each and exposing their mixed anomaly. Bosonization identifies momentum-winding T-duality, with a parity-projected operator flowing to a noninvertible topological defect. A nonperturbative norm-resolvent bound proves emergent dynamical gauge locality at finite chemical potential, while a doubled Chern-insulator parent reveals the duality's bulk origin and superconducting extensions reveal hidden compact symmetries.
  In 2D, the square $π$-flux Majorana model shares the Kitaev honeycomb model's single Dirac fermion and odd Pfaffian parity but supports sharp and exponentially local compact charges, the latter with nontrivial Chern topology. Relocalization retains Schwartz locality for asymptotically local gauging, while AIII/AII parents clarify bulk charge origin and parity-anomaly inflow. Two flavors yield compact $U(2)$, a quaternionic invariant, and asymptotically local non-Abelian gauging.
  In 3D, an exact mixed vector-axial flux response is derived, while a distinct model supports an exponentially local vector $U(1)$ charge with strong quaternionic topology. A nonlocal map makes the charge and Kramers symmetry onsite while preserving exponential Hamiltonian locality. For a compact $SU(2)$ Weyl doublet, a no-go theorem forbids translation-preserving Gaussian onsite relocalization retaining Weyl content and Hamiltonian locality.

title: Band-Selective Coupling to Charge Density Wave Fluctuations in Kagome Superconductors AV3Sb5
summary: The kagome superconductors AV3Sb5 (A=K, Rb, Cs) host multiband superconductivity (SC) within an unconventional charge density wave (CDW) parent phase, yet the relationship between the two remains unresolved. Through time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (tr-ARPES) experiments on CsV3Sb5 and KV3Sb5, we observe coherent band oscillations driven by coupling to a low-energy CDW amplitude mode at 3.1 THz. We find this coupling to be highly band-selective, differing by a factor of over 2 even between bands with dominant V-3d character. We reproduce these results with frozen-phonon density functional theory calculations, offering insight towards the relation between differing Fermi surface characters and our observed band selectivity. Furthermore, we observe differences in coupling channels between KV3Sb5 and CsV3Sb5. These results establish CDW amplitude mode fluctuations as a band-selective low-energy coupling channel that intimately contributes to the interplay between CDW and SC in the AV3Sb5 compounds.

title: Photocatalytic Water Splitting in GeC/ReS$_2$ van der Waals Heterostructures
summary: Photocatalytic water splitting is considered as one of the most promising approaches for the green hydrogen production. But the rapid recombination of photogenerated electron-hole pairs severely inhibits its photocatalytic efficiency. Construction of van der Waals heterostructures is a good way to suppress this recombination. However, in staggered band heterostructures, the charge transfer could occur either through the type-II or the direct Z-scheme mechanism. Therefore it is very important to identify which mechanism is dominant. In the present work, we systematically study the GeC/ReS$_2$ heterostructure using first-principles density functional theory (DFT). The system exhibits good thermodynamic, dynamic and thermal stability and an indirect band gap of 1.38 eV which greatly enhances the visible-light absorption. We find that the direct Z-scheme mechanism is the dominant interfacial charge transfer by analysing band alignment and Gibbs free energy pathways. The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) can be driven spontaneously in the pH range $4 \le \text{pH} \le 14$ under light irradiation for both type-II and Z-scheme pathways but the energy barrier is much lower for the Z-scheme mechanism. Moreover, the type-II mechanism is not suitable for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), but the Z-scheme mechanism can promote HER well in the entire pH range ($0 \le \text{pH} \le 14$). Remarkably, the strain-free (pristine) condition exhibits a solar-to-hydrogen (STH) efficiency of 41.40\%, well above the 10\% threshold for commercial viability. The STH efficiency is further enhanced to 60.68\% under a tensile strain of +6\%. To summarise, the Z-scheme strain-tunable GeC/ReS$_2$ heterostructure is a promising and efficient photocatalyst for overall water splitting.

title: On the computation of Green's function in layered elastic media
summary: We develop a recursive scheme for the computation of Green's function for time-harmonic elastic wave in three-dimensional layered media, based on a matrix basis representation in the Fourier domain and a classic interface reaction-transmission theory. With transversal rotational symmetry preserved, the scheme decouples the Green's function into SH waves and P-SV waves using five scalar functions, which are recursively solved at linear cost with respect to the number of total layers, regardless of the layers the source and target particles locate in. The resulting scheme leads to a stable numerical method ready for Hankel transform evaluation in the spatial domain, constituting a foundation for the analysis and efficient numerical simulation of elastic wave scattering in layered media.

title: Physical Realization of the Luczka Model: Inducing Interaction and Entanglement Between Spins
summary: The Luczka model describes the interaction of spins with a common bosonic environment in the pure-dephasing regime, in which the bosonic modes couple directly to only one spin component. Due to its specific form of interaction, the model is exactly solvable and has been widely used to describe spin decoherence and effective spin-spin interactions mediated by a common bosonic environment. However, to the best of our knowledge, its physical realization and the specific conditions under which such an interaction can be implemented have not yet been addressed. Here, we propose a physical realization of the Luczka spin-environment interaction by coupling the spin system to unidirectionally propagating, polarized electromagnetic radiation. In contrast to the original Luczka model, which allows an arbitrary angular distribution of photon wave vectors, our scheme gives a unidirectional photon flux with retaining a frequency distribution of the photons. As an illustrative application of the proposed realization, we investigate spin-entanglement dynamics for coherent, single-mode thermal, and Ohmic

title: Moiré-enabled polariton control in large-angle twisted bilayer graphene
summary: Twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) is commonly viewed through two limiting regimes: strongly correlated flat bands near the magic angle and nearly decoupled Dirac cones at large twist angles. Here we explore the intermediate regime. Using hyperbolic plasmon-phonon polaritons (HP$^{3}$) to probe the dynamical electronic response, we investigate bilayer graphene from AB stacking to $5.5^\circ$ TBG. We identify a narrow density window in which the HP$^{3}$ wavelength becomes strongly gate tunable. The window opens when doping suppresses Landau damping and a coherent graphene plasmon emerges. It closes at a second crossover, which appears only above $4^\circ$ and shifts systematically with twist angle. Continuum-model and electrodynamic calculations trace this second crossover to hybridization between the central and remote moiré bands, which weakens the density dependence of the Drude response. The resulting polaritonic tunability is concentrated within a twist-angle-selected density window and produces total wavelength changes approaching $90\%$. Our results demonstrate that remote moiré bands reshape the collective electrodynamics of TBG far from the magic-angle regime and establish large-angle TBG as a platform for gate-reconfigurable mid-infrared polaritons and material cavities.

title: Parton Physics in the Schwinger Model from Matrix Product States
summary: Parton distribution functions (PDFs) and light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) encode the non-perturbative structure of hadrons in terms of their partonic constituents. They are defined through matrix elements containing parton operators that are connected by a Wilson line along a light-front direction, which makes them difficult to access in Euclidean lattice calculations. We demonstrate how parton functions can be directly obtained in Minkowski space using the Hamiltonian framework. We compute fermion and antifermion PDFs, LCDAs, and decay constants of the vector meson in the Schwinger model for several fermion masses. States in Hilbert space are efficiently represented by tensor networks, with an expressivity that is systematically controlled by a bond dimension. The light-front Wilson line is implemented as a stepwise evolution on the lattice that alternates spatial shifts of an external charge with Trotterized time-evolution steps acting on a matrix product state. All systematic uncertainties are quantified by varying and extrapolating in the lattice spacing, volume, bond dimension, gauge-field truncation, and Trotter step width. The slow growth of the entanglement entropy makes moderate bond dimensions sufficient, which supports the feasibility of using tensor networks for computing light-front matrix elements in more general settings. We confirm that the computed distributions fulfill the expected normalizations, momentum sum rules, and symmetry properties.

title: Condensates and Edge Effects in the Generalised Takayasu Model
summary: Recently, in the 1D Takayasu Mass Model (MM) of diffusion-aggregation with input, large condensates and a novel power law were observed in simulations, and later characterised exactly. We extend these studies to the Takayasu model with generalised input, and provide a relation to translate the distribution function of the MM to any model with a space and time independent injection process. In the 1D Charge Model (CM) of a system of size $L$, where $q=+1$ and $-1$ charge monomers are injected with equal probability at each site in each time step, there is a power law distribution of cluster charge $P(q)\sim |q|^{-5/3}$. This distribution cuts off at $|q|\sim L^{3/2}$ in the steady state for long times $t\gg L^2$ and a large charge condensate forms with a net charge between $-\sqrt{Lt}$ and $\sqrt{Lt}$. A distance dependent distribution function is observed around the charge condensate and near open boundaries, both of which act like an edge in the system, analogous to the observations in the MM. The charge distribution measured at a distance $x$ from the edge transitions from the previously known CM bulk power law $P(q)\sim |q|^{-5/3}$ for small clusters ($|q|< x^{3/2}$), to a novel power law $P(q)\sim |q|^{-7/3}$ for larger clusters ($|q|>x^{3/2}$). In the 1D Pair Injection Model (PIM), where $+1$ and $-1$ charge monomers are injected simultaneously at adjacent sites, the power law distribution $P(q)\sim |q|^{-2}$ cuts off at $|q|\sim L$ in the steady state for long times, and no large growing condensate is formed. We still observe a distance dependent distribution measured from the largest clusters, or an open boundary, with a bulk power law $P(q)\sim |q|^{-2}$ for small clusters ($|q|< x$), and an edge power law $P(q)\sim |q|^{-3}$ for larger clusters ($|q >x$).

title: Non-integer high harmonic generation from many-body nonadiabatic gating
comment: 10 pages main text, 5 figures, 43 pages supplementary information
summary: High harmonic generation (HHG) in solids typically produces a rigid frequency comb locked to exact integer multiples of the drive photon energy. In strongly correlated materials, however, the light field can dynamically transform the electronic state on the timescale of harmonic generation itself, potentially violating this rule. Here, we report giant blueshifted, non-integer HHG in a cuprate Mott insulator Sr$_2$CuO$_3$ produced by mid-infrared excitations. Concurrent transient reflectivity measurements and time-dependent exact-diagonalization simulations of a driven Hubbard model support a many-body temporal gating mechanism that suppresses light emission on the trailing edge of the pulse, thereby blueshifting radiated harmonics in the frequency domain. Our findings establish HHG emission energy as a sensitive probe of quantum many-body dynamics and pave the way for exploration and manipulation of correlated electronic phases of matter with strong-field spectroscopy.

title: Tunneling signatures of the Lifshitz transition in a superconducting vortex
summary: The Caroli-de Gennes-Matricon states bound to a vortex line in a clean type-II superconductor form one-dimensional minibands that disperse along the vortex. The lowest miniband is separated from the Fermi level by a minigap $E_0\simΔ^2/E_F$. A magnetic field shifts the minibands of the two spin projections in opposite directions. At the threshold field $B^*$ the Zeeman energy equals $E_0$. Estimates for FeSe place $B^*$ at a few tesla. The lowest miniband of one spin projection then crosses the Fermi level, and a spin-polarized one-dimensional Fermi sea forms inside the vortex core. We develop the theory of tunneling spectra across this Lifshitz transition. We solve the Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations numerically in the quantum limit for all momenta along the vortex and compute the local density of states with thermal and instrumental broadening. The zero-bias conductance at the vortex center is absent below $B^*$. It has a maximum near $B^*$ with the inverse-square-root field dependence of a one-dimensional van Hove singularity and decreases at higher fields. The next miniband produces a second onset at a finite distance from the center. The zero-bias signal is carried by one spin projection at the center and by the opposite one in the surrounding ring. We then project the screened electron interaction onto the filled miniband. The resulting Luttinger parameter is close to unity, so the core hosts a weakly interacting one-dimensional Fermi gas. Its quasiparticles relax through three-particle collisions in analogy with thermalization in quantum wires and at quantum Hall edges. The corresponding relaxation rates are established analytically.

title: Magic-layer scenario for predicting non-van der Waals two-dimensional materials: The case of double-layer honeycomb structures
summary: A magic number is a specific size of a van der Waals (vdW) cluster that shows pronounced stability compared to adjacent sizes, and therefore magic clusters are preferentially formed in experiments. We apply the ``magic-layer'' concept to identify non-vdW two-dimensional (2D) materials that are difficult to exfoliate from their parent 3D crystals. As a case, we study the stability of thin films in III-V, II-VI, I-VII, and Mn-based compounds using first-principles calculations. By calculating excess energies for various thicknesses, we find significant stabilization reflecting the formation of double-layer honeycomb structures at specific thicknesses. The stability measure based on the magic-layer concept can distinguish the experimentally synthesized systems from the experimentally unrealized systems, which serves as a key descriptor for predicting the realization of non-vdW 2D materials.

title: Cantor spectrum at a fixed Diophantine frequency
summary: We establish that the spectrum of one-frequency analytic quasiperiodic Schrodinger operators exhibits Cantor structure in the regime of positive Lyapunov exponents for every fixed Diophantine frequency. The proof follows the general strategy of the gap construction by Goldstein and the second author, but avoids the elimination of double and triple resonances used in the original argument. A novel ingredient is the use of Holder continuity of the integrated density of states (IDS) to exclude energies at which eigenvalue parametrizations in finite volume have small slopes. We also use a linear bound in the volume on the number of zeros of Dirichlet determinants, and a pigeonholing argument to obtain lower bounds on the distances between eigenvalues. The crossing of two translated Rellich functions with opposite slopes produces a local maximum whose eigenfunctions have exponentially small boundary values. Together with finite volume eigenvalue separation, this forces the DOS mass to concentrate near the maximum. However, on an interval of constancy of the acceleration, the Lyapunov exponent is analytic, and hence the DOS is Lipschitz there. This ultimately leads to a contradiction near the maximum.

title: Beyond Quantum Mechanics: From Nonlinear to Emergent and Solitonic Approaches
comment: Master's thesis in Physics, Sapienza University of Rome, defended on 17 November 2026. Supervisor: Prof. Claudio Conti. 137 pages
summary:
This thesis investigates the role of nonlinearity in approaches beyond standard quantum mechanics, following a path from modifications of quantum dynamics to the possibility of an emergent statistical description. We first examine Weinberg's nonlinear formulation and its implications for the statistical interpretation of quantum states. We then discuss de Broglie-Bohm theory and the Madelung formulation, which provide a framework for comparing guided trajectories with ensemble descriptions involving momentum fluctuations. The Hall-Reginatto exact uncertainty approach identifies the fluctuation energy associated with the quantum potential.
  We then investigate whether quantum dynamics can emerge from the collective statistics of solitons in a fluctuating background, using a Galilean formulation of the complex sine-Gordon model. Within a weak-noise approximation, we identify a regime in which the statistics of the soliton centres reproduce the Schr{ö}dinger equation, with an effective action scale determined by the background fluctuations. This correspondence is established for Gaussian ensembles and potentials at most quadratic.
  These results provide a concrete setting for exploring how quantum dynamics can emerge as a statistical description of underlying nonlinear field dynamics.

title: Excess noise and electron-phonon energy transfer in Au wires: Length and temperature effects
summary: As a mesoscopic diffusive wire at low temperatures is driven out of equilibrium by a current, excess noise is observed compared to the equilibrium Johnson-Nyquist fluctuations. The expected form of the excess noise varies depending on the relative rates of wire traversal, electron-electron inelastic energy transfer, and electron-phonon inelastic energy transfer. We measure noise as a function of bias current in diffusive Au nanowires on SiO2/Si with lengths ranging from sub-μm to 30 μm and temperatures from 3 K to 50 K, to map out the interplay between charge shot noise and the crossover to electron self-heating and phonon-dominated noise suppression. As expected qualitatively, shot noise is suppressed with increasing wire length and substrate temperature, as electron-phonon scattering is of increasing importance. In long wires, the simple model of electron-phonon energy loss known to be quantitatively effective below a few Kelvin underpredicts the excess noise in the high bias, high temperature limit. This issue is more severe in wires on SiO2/Si than on bare Si, implying that interfacial thermal conduction must be considered in the thermal path even at comparatively high temperatures.

title: Intrinsic Soft Function in the Continuum and Physical Mass Limit from Lattice QCD
summary: The intrinsic soft function is a universal nonperturbative ingredient of transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) factorization. Despite substantial progress in lattice QCD studies, a determination with simultaneous control of the continuum, physical-pion-mass, and infinite-momentum limits has remained unavailable. In this work we present the first lattice determination incorporating all these limits within large-momentum effective theory, extracting the intrinsic soft function from a light-meson form factor and quasi-TMD wave functions. A key advance is the use of power-counting-guided axial-vector interpolators, which substantially improve the signal and enable a direct calculation at the physical pion mass. Combined with results from six ensembles spanning four lattice spacings, this improvement allows a precise determination extending to $b_\perp\simeq1.1~\mathrm{fm}$, while remaining consistent with perturbative predictions at short distances. The resulting transverse-distance dependence exhibits an approximately exponential decay, with the decay rate being characterized by an effective scale $Λ\simeq0.7~\mathrm{GeV}$ at $μ=2~\mathrm{GeV}$, providing a quantitative benchmark for nonperturbative Wilson-line dynamics and essential input for precision TMD studies.

title: What time is it in Assembly Space? Cronin and Walker's "The Physics of Causation" fails elementary dimensional analysis (Comment on arXiv:2601.00515)
comment: Comment on arXiv:2601.00515, 2.5 pages, no comments
summary: Cronin and Walker claim that causation is quantified by an ``assembly index'', a count of the steps needed to build an object. Remarkably, they equate ``continuous time (as measured by clocks)'' to a multiple of the index, which is a dimensionless number. Their argument treats one parameter as simultaneously a rate, a time interval, and a pure number, and provides no timescale to convert index to clock time. This dimensional incoherence betrays, at best, an ill-conceived and ill-formed theory, and fatally undermines two central claims. First, the exponential weighting at the heart of what they call the assembly equation can be obtained only by supplying a timescale, which they never do, or by recasting clock time as a dimensionless count of assembly steps. In the latter case, their ``derivation'' trivially reduces to Bernoulli's seventeenth-century compound-interest limit. Second, lacking rates or energy scales, their account cannot predict how quickly, or under what conditions, anything forms, and yet formation ``in finite time'' is their criterion for distinguishing spontaneous from ``selected'' objects. Assembly theory is thus incapable of addressing causation.

title: Origin of quadrupolar order in the 5d$^1$ double perovskite Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$
comment: 9 pages, 5 figures + 11 pages, 1 figure of Supplemental
summary: Despite extensive experimental and theoretical studies of quadrupolar order in Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$, the microscopic origin and relative energy scales of the interactions driving it remain unresolved. In particular, the observed ferroic ordering of the $z^2$ quadrupole has remained difficult to explain, as the relative contributions of superexchange, classical quadrupole-quadrupole interactions, vibronic couplings, and virtual excitations to higher-energy levels have not been established quantitatively. Here, we determine all these interactions from first principles and solve the resulting microscopic Hamiltonian. The calculated ground state reproduces the experimentally observed quadrupolar order parameters and the associated structural distortions with quantitative accuracy. Disentangling the individual contributions, we find that ferroic $z^2$ order originates from a linear-quartic coupling, generated by virtual excitations to the $J_{\mathrm{eff}}$= 1/2 doublet and driven by vibronic interactions. Our results establish the hierarchy of microscopic interactions underlying quadrupolar order in Ba$_2$MgReO$_6$ and provide a unified $ab \ initio$ description of its coupled electronic and lattice degrees of freedom.

title: Eigenvalue-based computation of Richardson pairing spectra and finite-size thermodynamics
summary: We present a numerical workflow for the reduced BCS Richardson model, combining the eigenvalue-based Bethe equations, Baxter-polynomial reconstruction, and complex root finding. Newton-Raphson iteration solves the nonlinear equations for the eigenvalue-based variables; a linear system yields the polynomial coefficients, and Laguerre iteration with polynomial deflation extracts the rapidities. We apply the procedure to equally spaced, quadratic, and hydrogen-like non-degenerate single-particle spectra as the pairing strength varies. For finite systems, we calculate canonical observables from the complete seniority-zero spectrum and check benchmark spectra against exact diagonalization. In an eight-level, four-pair system with a hydrogen-like spectrum, the heat capacity has two maxima at weak coupling. With increasing coupling, the low-temperature maximum shifts upward and the high-temperature maximum downward; the latter ceases to be a distinct local maximum near $g\simeq0.03515$ in the units used. The equally spaced benchmark instead has a single dominant maximum over the coupling interval displayed for that spectrum. This comparison illustrates how single-particle level spacings can shape finite-size thermal response. The C++ code is publicly available; numerical instabilities remain possible near ill-conditioned configurations and at larger sizes.

title: Accelerating Equivariant Interatomic Potentials for Molecular Dynamics through Radial tabulation and Kernel Fusion
comment: 47 pages including references, 6 Figures and 4 Tables in main manuscript
summary: Equivariant machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) achieve near-quantum-chemical accuracy, but their computational cost and GPU memory footprint restrict molecular dynamics (MD) at extended length and time scales. Even when the tensor product (TP) is accelerated, both bottlenecks remain governed by evaluating and storing per-edge radial weights in the NequIP convolution. We introduce JET-MLIPs (Joint-Kernel Equivariant Convolution with Tabulated Radial Weights for MLIP simulation), a GPU backend applicable to pretrained NequIP-family potentials without retraining. JET-MLIPs replaces the radial multilayer perceptron (MLP) with a piecewise cubic Hermite table and fuses table lookup, spherical harmonics, TP and neighbor aggregation into a single kernel, eliminating per-edge radial-weight and MLP-intermediate storage during force evaluation. Across 15 released potentials from SevenNet, MACE, NequIP-OAM, Nequix and EquFlash on a 5632-atom liquid electrolyte, LAMMPS MD attains 1.5-5.9$\times$ step-time speed-ups and 2.4-24$\times$ peak memory reductions relative to each family's existing TP-accelerated backend on a single H200 GPU while preserving single-precision (fp32) accuracy and dynamical stability. These reductions enable multi-nanosecond transport-property simulations of roughly $10^4$-atom systems on a single GPU and broaden access to large-scale equivariant MLIP MD on widely available GPUs.

title: Field-Dependent Kinetics, Exact Kinks, and a Moduli-Space Route from Self-Dual Yang-Mills Theory
summary: We study scalar-field models in 1+1 dimensions with field-dependent kinetic coefficients, motivated by self-dual Yang-Mills (SDYM) theory as a generator of integrable equations. We derive the Euler-Lagrange equation, traveling-wave reduction, and first integral, and solve the inverse problem: given a kinetic structure and a prescribed tanh kink, which potential makes it exact? A quadratic spatial deformation with a canonical temporal sector yields a sextic potential. We obtain: (i) a closed-form kink energy with a Bogomolny-type formulation, independent of the odd parameter, which nonetheless shapes the energy density asymmetrically; (ii) vacuum curvature relations tying the spectrum to the kinetic function at the vacua; (iii) two propositions on speed families, plus a lemma showing single-speed data probe only one combination of the kinetic functions; (iv) a unified admissibility analysis in which positivity of the spatial kinetic function controls hyperbolicity, the potential bound along the kink, and the vacuum masses; (v) a self-adjoint fluctuation operator with a closed-form potential whose asymptotes are the vacuum masses, an exact translation zero mode, and numerical spectra with no negative mode on the admissible region, evidence for spectral stability. Exact SDYM reductions yield integrable equations, whereas the deformed model is generically non-integrable and cannot be an exact reduction. The correct bridge is the moduli-space route: SDYM reduces to the Bogomolny equations, whose BPS monopole and dyon dynamics produce field-dependent kinetic terms; any smooth one-dimensional moduli metric expands, to second order, to the quadratic model studied here, and the Taub-NUT metric of well-separated dyons gives an explicit realization. Full identification of the sextic potential within a specific gauge-theory moduli dynamics remains open and is formulated as a research program.

title: A counterexample to the Ho-Hsieh VQCS saturation conjecture
summary: We show that there exists a 4-qubit state that can be prepared by a variational quantum-classical simulation (VQCS) circuit ansatz containing 3 layers, but not with 2 layers. This disproves the strong form of a conjecture presented by Ho and Hsieh stating that the expressivity of VQCS on $L$ qubits saturates at $L/2$ layers. The weak form of the conjecture concerning the preparation of the ground state remains open.

title: Interface and film engineering for improved spin-charge interconversion in sputtered GeTe nanodevices
summary: Spin-logic devices promise non-volatile logic-in-memory computing with ultra-low power consumption, offering a route to circumvent the von Neumann bottleneck. Magnetoelectric and ferroelectric spin-orbit (MESO/FESO) devices, however, require spin-charge interconversion materials that combine a large output signal with properties that survive nanoscale integration. Tellurides are particularly fragile in this respect, as processing readily introduces defects that degrade their spin-charge interconversion properties. Here we demonstrate room-temperature spin-charge interconversion in patterned FESO nanoscale devices based on sputtered GeTe, with feature sizes down to 100 nm. By introducing a Ti interfacial layer between the CoFe electrode and GeTe, and by using GeTe films of improved crystalline quality, we increase the interconversion output signal from 3 mΩ to 24 mΩ, exceeding values reported for platinum at comparable device size. These results establish large-scale-deposited GeTe as a viable material platform for spin-logic devices and identify interface quality and film crystallinity as key levers for optimizing their performance.

title: Bound-state preparation in strongly coupled theories
summary: Many quantum simulation tasks, including scattering in quantum field theories and effective non-relativistic theories, require the preparation of asymptotic states. Such a state, which may be a bound state, is typically the lowest-lying excited state in some sector of Hilbert space. At weak coupling these states can often be prepared adiabatically by beginning with the free theory, but this is not generally feasible in strongly coupled theories. We detail a family of algorithms for preparing composite states in strongly coupled theories, including non-Abelian gauge theories, by using weakly coupled auxiliary fields. These methods do not require quantum phase estimation. We demonstrate the method numerically, via classical simulation, on nonrelativistic theories in one spatial dimension. We estimate the yield of this method applied to $J/ψ$ production in quantum chromodynamics.

title: Localization in one-dimensional magnetic quasicrystals
summary: The celebrated Aubry-André-Harper model undergoes a metal-insulator transition akin to Anderson localization due to an energetic competition between nearest-neighbor hopping and a quasiperiodic on-site potential. In this work, we consider the problem of a one-dimensional lattice subject to a quasiperiodic external field, where the topology of the underlying graph mediates the competition between insulating and conducting phases. In particular, we present examples for which all dispersive eigenstates are critically localized, as well as models in which they are exponentially localized. We also demonstrate the coexistence of these phenomena with an extensive set of degenerate finitely supported eigenstates forming a flat band. Finally, we construct models with exactly solvable mobility edges arising only from graph structure. Going beyond these single-particle results, we show---using exact-diagonalization calculations of the bosonic dynamics---that, as in the conventional Aubry-André-Harper case, on-site interactions drive localized eigenstates toward extendedness. Our results provide a framework for exploring how magnetic interference and interactions jointly constrain transport in quasiperiodic lattices.

title: Ground state and thermal phase diagrams of the magnetized spin-$1/2$ XXZ antiferromagnet on the triangular lattice
summary: The spin-1/2 XXZ antiferromagnet on the triangular lattice in a magnetic field is a paradigmatic frustrated quantum magnet, yet its ground-state phase diagram at generic anisotropy and its thermal phase structure remain incompletely understood. Here, using infinite density-matrix renormalization group, infinite projected entangled-pair operator, and exponential tensor renormalization group methods, supported by exact diagonalization, we resolve both issues. At zero temperature, we map the phase diagram continuously from the Ising limit to the Heisenberg point and find that the nonclassical $Ψ$ supersolid is a stable phase just below saturation at all anisotropies studied: it borders the one-third-magnetization up-up-down plateau directly in the strongly easy-axis regime and the semiclassical $V$ phase toward the Heisenberg point. In the strongly easy-axis regime, we uncover an intrinsically finite-temperature bond-nematic phase above the zero-temperature plateau--$Ψ$ boundary, in which the three bond directions become spontaneously inequivalent without transverse spin coherence or three-sublattice order. A hard-core-boson mapping reveals its origin: once thermal fluctuations destroy phase coherence, the field-doped holes settle on domain walls of the local up-up-down order, which are stabilized by quantum kink delocalization and aligned by its $Z_3$ registry. Our results call for reexamining high-field states in triangular-lattice cobaltates such as Na$_2$BaCo(PO$_4$)$_2$ and K$_2$Co(SeO$_3$)$_2$.

title: Majorana flat bands from mirror-particle-hole antisymmetry
summary: Majorana flat bands, zero modes across the whole edge Brillouin zone, usually rest on chiral symmetry. We show that a fully gapped class-D superconductor can host such a flat band without chiral symmetry or time reversal, provided its superconducting gap is odd under a mirror and translation along the edge is preserved. Combined with particle--hole conjugation, the mirror forms an antiunitary antisymmetry that squares to $+1$ and preserves the momentum along the edge, so it fixes the Kitaev index of every slice of fixed edge momentum. In a gapped bulk, this slice index cannot change with the edge momentum, and the edge zero modes form a band across the whole edge Brillouin zone. We construct a four-band model with exactly these symmetries, a helical $p$-wave superconductor with Rashba coupling in an in-plane exchange field, from which no term can be removed without restoring an additional symmetry. On the mirror lines, its two mirror sectors are exact Kitaev chains. This yields a closed-form phase diagram. Besides the flat band, the model hosts a phase with two Majoranas at each end of a wire, although its class-D index is trivial, and a second-order phase with Majorana corner modes. The spectral localizer detects all these indices in real space, directly on finite-size samples as relevant for experiments. On open rectangular flakes of two widths, it reproduces the phase diagram even though translational symmetry is broken. In the nodal regions, its reading depends on the flake size, so they are left unread. The readings persist under disorder several times the bulk gap. Without translation along the edge, the symmetries protect no more than Majorana parities, and we quantify the signatures that remain specific to the antisymmetry. A minimal model of magnetic adatoms on a triplet superconductor realizes the flat-band and second-order phases.

title: From Weighted Frontier d-States to Geometric Descriptors for Atomically Dispersed Catalysts at the Molecule-Solid Crossover
summary: Atomically dispersed catalysts exhibit molecule-solid crossover character when localized metal orbitals hybridize with support-derived bands, a regime not fully captured by either a d-band-center description or a frontier-orbital picture. We establish an electronic-to-geometric framework for oxygen reduction across fourteen metals. N-to-P substitution in M-N4 sites raises theoretical onset potentials in 13 systems, with Rh-N3P reaching 0.88 V, comparable to the Pt(111) benchmark. Scaling relations reduce *OOH, *O, and *OH thermodynamics to $Δ$G*OH. M-N4 follows a dyz-dominated frontier-orbital picture, whereas M-N3P requires a weighted frontier d-state representation built from adsorption-relevant orbitals and their occupancies. The resulting $ε$WFDS correlates with $Δ$G*OH at $R^2$ = 0.92, compared with 0.83 for the d-band center and 0.64 for the frontier-orbital. The identified roles of orbital occupancy and local coordination suggest an interpretable geometric descriptor, $ζ$M-N3P = nd/rM-P, that predicts $Δ$G*OH at $R^2$ = 0.96. The ORR volcano analysis identifies strong-binding systems and motivates axial oxygen coordination. This design raises onset potentials by 0.70-2.46 V, and the M-N3PO descriptor predicts $Δ$G*OH at $R^2$ = 0.91. By bridging frontier-orbital and d-band-center descriptions, the framework provides a physically grounded electronic representation and a geometry-based screening route compatible with machine-learned interatomic potentials.

title: Exact transport exponents for random mosaic operators
summary: We determine the exponentially time-averaged transport exponents of period-two random mosaic operators, with zero potential on the even sites and iid potential on the odd sites. For every bounded, strictly positive, nonconstant single-site law, on one event of probability one, $β_f^-(q)=β_f^+(q)=\max\{0,2/3-ν_H(f)/(3q)\}$ for all nonzero finitely supported states $f$ and all $q>0$. The positive odd integer $ν_H(f)$ is determined by divisibility by $H$ and cancellation against the bounded zero-energy solution. In particular, the large-moment exponent is $2/3$ for every such state, while point sources on the two sublattices have second-moment growth powers $1$ and $1/3$. We obtain matching resolvent bounds by retaining the vanishing orders of two polynomial source channels through the singular normalization at zero energy. We also prove deterministic lower bounds for every bounded positive configuration. No density assumption is imposed on the law.

title: Certifying closed labs in device-independent tests of indefinite causality
comment: 10 pages + 14 pages of Suppl. Materials; 4 figures + 2 in the Suppl. Materials
summary: Indefinite causal order allows processes in which the order of events is not predetermined, enabling information-processing advantages unattainable with fixed causal structures. A long-standing open problem is whether such processes can be certified without trusting the devices used to demonstrate them, analogous to device-independent certifications of Bell nonlocality. Causal inequalities offer a route towards this goal, since their violation is intended to rule out all definite causal structures. However, fully device-independent certification of indefinite causal order remains elusive. The difficulty lies in the closed laboratories assumption, which requires each party to interact at most once with systems that mediate communication. Without this assumption, ordinary two-way communication can reproduce causal-inequality violations without involving indefinite causal order. Yet an untrusted device could violate the assumption by interacting with the mediating system more than once, while remaining undetected from input-output statistics alone. We address this loophole by embedding a minimal set of additional experimental components into a certification scheme. These elements probabilistically probe the underlying process, enabling the closed laboratories assumption to be validated directly within the protocol. Our framework provides operationally meaningful minimal-assumption tests of indefinite causal order, clarifying its distinction from nonlocality and paving the way for cryptographic and self-testing applications.

title: Moiré-Induced Interlayer Electron-Phonon Coupling in Graphene/hBN Superlattices
summary: Electron-phonon coupling (EPC) plays a vital role in the electrical and optical properties of materials, ranging from superconductivity to charge dynamics. In moiré superlattices, out-of-plane vibrations can modulate the moiré potential and enhance interlayer EPC. Here we report the first direct observation of a resonance arising from coupling between moiré electronic excitations and phonons in graphene-based moiré superlattices. Using Fourier-transform infrared photocurrent spectroscopy, we detect the nominally silent hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) out-of-plane optical (ZO) phonon as a pronounced absorption peak. The phonon interferes with moiré flat-band excitations to form a characteristic Fano resonance. Displacement field-dependent measurements confirm that the feature originates from coupling to the moiré electronic continuum rather than simple zone folding. We further observe similar resonances in devices with different graphene layer numbers and twist configurations. This enhanced EPC provides a pathway for understanding and controlling emerging quantum phenomena, such as superconductivity, and engineering novel optoelectronic devices.

title: Prospects and limitations of adaptive variational quantum algorithms for lattice field theories: a case study in 2+1 dimensions
summary: The variational quantum algorithm ADAPT-VQE has previously been used to prepare the vacuum of lattice gauge theories in $1+1D$. In this paper, we study whether it extends to higher dimensions. We identify two general limitations of ADAPT-VQE. First, if the qubit Hamiltonian and the initial state are real, i.e., invariant under qubit-level time-reversal, all real-valued pool operators have vanishing gradients and are never selected. Second, the algorithm can converge to excited eigenstates. We illustrate both limitations, also providing examples from literature, and present a first application of ADAPT-VQE to a lattice field theory in $2+1D$, namely free Wilson fermions, where both obstacles occur. Adding charge conjugation symmetry to the operator pool improves the results, and combining different pools with suitable initial states recovers the ground and first excited states over the full mass range. These findings give practical guidelines for applying ADAPT-VQE to lattice field theories beyond $1+1D$.

title: From Growth Inhibition to Fluctuations: Testing an Ising Model of Bacterial Responses to Antibiotics
summary: Complex networks of biochemical reactions have been proposed to exhibit emergent cooperativity that can be described by an effective Ising model, with a small number of parameters encoding collective interactions. Here this mapping is experimentally tested using the response of three bacterial species to a range of antibiotics acting on different cellular targets. The Ising description is compared to the conventional Hill model, examining both the mean growth-rate response and, importantly, its population growth-rate heterogeneity (PGRH). While both models describe the mean growth-rate dependence on antibiotic concentration comparably well, we find that the Ising model provides a markedly better description of PGRH, offering an additional and more stringent test of the collective description. The fitted Ising interaction strength is systematically related to the Hill exponent and increases with the functional distance of the antibiotic target from the protein-production machinery. These results provide experimental support for describing complex biochemical reaction networks through effective cooperative Ising interactions, and suggest that the collective response of bacterial growth to antibiotics reflects the organization of the underlying metabolic network.

title: High-density correlation energy of the electron gas
summary: The high-density expansion of the correlation energy per electron of the unpolarized three-dimensional electron gas, $ε_c = A\ln r_s + B + C r_s\ln r_s + D r_s + \dots$, is used in many approximations to the correlation functional of density-functional theory. The coefficients $A$, $B$ and $C$ are known exactly. We revisit the three diagram classes used to estimate $D$, namely bare rings, rings with one first-order exchange insertion, and third-order diagrams with three distinct momentum transfers. Their sum is $-0.0077880(9)$ Ha per electron, compared with the earlier estimate of $-0.010$ Ha. The difference comes mainly from the coupling-constant weighting of the exchange rings in the calculation of Carr and Maradudin. At order $r_s^2$, seven contributions to the single-logarithm coefficient $E_1$ sum to $(3.653 \pm 0.010)\times 10^{-3}$ Ha per electron. The three long-wavelength contributions to the double-logarithm coefficient $E_2$ sum to $α^2(36π^2 - 208\ln 2 - 221)/(192π^4) \approx -1.433\times 10^{-4}$ Ha per electron, where $α= (4/9π)^{1/3}$. Available diffusion Monte Carlo energies at $r_s = 0.5$ cannot distinguish between the two estimates of $D$.

title: Superconductivity with valley-imbalanced Fermi surfaces in thick rhombohedral graphene
summary: Superconductivity in spin-polarized metals challenges conventional opposite-spin pairing, particularly when a magnetic field strengthens rather than suppresses it. In graphene, the additional valley degree of freedom broadens the possible pairing channels, making the valley occupation of the parent metal central to understanding such superconductivity. Here we report in-plane-field-enhanced superconductivity in hBN-aligned 17-layer rhombohedral graphene. Normal-state quantum oscillations reveal unequal Fermi pockets consistent with a valley-imbalanced, spin-polarized parent metal. Calculations show that the parent electron pocket is predominantly localized on the bottom surface and largely preserved by electrostatic screening as additional Fermi pockets emerge. Superconductivity persists in this regime but is suppressed when carriers are polarized toward the hBN-aligned surface, where the parent bands undergo strong moire reconstruction. An adjacent nonlinear metallic response evolves continuously into superconducting critical-current features and persists above the superconducting transition temperature. The combination of valley imbalance and in-plane-field-enhanced superconductivity motivates a phenomenological magnon-assisted equal-spin intervalley pairing scenario. These findings provide experimental constraints on pairing in valley-imbalanced metals and open a route to testing magnetic pairing mechanisms through layer-selective control of the parent electronic states.

title: Emergent Electric-Field-Tunable $p$-Wave Magnetism in Twisted Bilayer NiPS$_3$
summary: A perpendicular electric field can reorient a momentum-space spin texture without changing the local magnetic configuration. In this Letter, we investigate this mechanism in a $21^\circ$-twisted $\mathrm{NiPS}_3$ bilayer with zigzag order and coplanar, nonparallel layer Néel vectors. In the ideal nonrelativistic limit, an antiunitary in-plane half-translation enforces opposite-spin pairing at opposite momenta, while a layer-exchanging twofold operation pins the leading $p$-wave spin splitting to a crystallographic direction. A perpendicular layer bias lifts this orientational constraint while preserving the antiunitary symmetry, allowing a transverse component of the splitting vector. First-principles calculations show gate-dependent reorientation and deformation of spin-resolved isoenergy contours. Wannier-based linear-response calculations further reveal field-activated diagonal spin conductivities and a polarity-dependent tilt in the angular profile of the transverse spin-current response. The spin-texture axis, dispersion axes, and transport-response axis are distinct quantities governed by the same symmetry reduction. These results identify layer bias as a route to controlling odd-parity spin textures and spin-current anisotropy, provided that the coplanar magnetic state remains stable.

title: Group classification of a class of systems of nonlinear diffusion equations. I
comment: Revised and corrected version of the article published in Ukr. Math. J. 78, 40 (2026). In particular, the group classification of the first subclass has been corrected and substantially refined
summary: We study the Lie symmetries of a class of systems of (1 + 1)-dimensional nonlinear diffusion equations. The equivalence algebra and the kernel of the maximal Lie invariance algebras of this class are found. We prove that there exist exactly nine inequivalent subclasses of this class for which the corresponding diffusion systems admit Lie symmetry extensions. We also carry out the exhaustive group classification of the systems of nonlinear diffusion equations from the first subclass.

title: Ground-State Chiral Quantum Clusters
summary: Quantum time crystals are states of matter that spontaneously break time translation symmetry, extending the notion of crystalline order to time. While their out-of-equilibrium version has been successfully realized by periodic driving, the equilibrium counterpart remains elusive. Here we introduce "ground-state chiral quantum clusters": self-bound many-body ground states supporting a persistent current. We provide a minimal field theory describing these states, and an exact microscopic realization via the attractive anyonic Lieb-Liniger model on a ring. In the latter, the ground-state density-density correlator exhibits the Talbot effect, with a soliton-like profile that periodically disperses and revives while drifting indefinitely along the ring, realizing persistent motion at equilibrium. Possible experimental probes are discussed.

title: Environmentally assisted transport in a diamond chain
summary: We study quantum transport in a diamond chain coupled to Markovian reservoirs at its boundaries. The system is subject to uniform dephasing and an external magnetic field threading a flux $Φ$ per plaquette. We derive exact analytical solutions for $Φ=0$ and $Φ=π$. We show that in the all-bands-flat regime at $Φ=π$, dephasing destroys Aharonov-Bohm caging, leading to environment-assisted quantum transport. Our results demonstrate that coupling a flat-band system to a dissipative environment provides a viable route for controlling transport in regimes where coherent dynamics alone would result in complete localization.

title: Upper and lower bounds for the critical point of the three-dimensional Ising model
comment: 37 pages, 6 figures. Code, certificates and logs: https://github.com/whyihaveyou/ising3d-critical-interval (archived at doi:10.5281/zenodo.24487984)
summary: We prove that the critical point $K_c$ of the nearest-neighbour Ising ferromagnet on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ satisfies $0.2164203058<K_c<0.2293910295$, equivalently $1.541630483<e^{2K_c}<1.582145851$, with both endpoints given by explicit rational numbers. To our knowledge these are the sharpest rigorous bounds available. They improve the classical bounds of Fisher (1967) and of Fröhlich, Simon and Spencer (1976), narrowing the rigorously known interval by a factor of about 3.5, and the interval contains the numerical estimate of the critical point. For the lower bound we refine Fisher's self-avoiding-walk argument. A shortest path in the high-temperature expansion forbids all bonds spanned by its vertices, and the resulting gain is estimated through local correlation integrals and summed over paths by a finite-memory transfer bound. As a by-product, the connective constant of $\mathbb{Z}^3$ is shown to be at most $4.73195$. For the upper bound we prove an infrared bound whose coefficient involves the nearest-neighbour correlation. We keep the zero Fourier mode as an unknown and force it to be positive by exact local relations for the spins on a small shell. The finite inequalities entering the proof are verified in exact rational arithmetic, and the passage to the thermodynamic limit is proved analytically.

title: A fermionic framework for quantum machine learning benchmarks
summary: We present a framework for building and benchmarking scalable machine learning (ML) models based on simulating free-fermion systems. Our fermionic ML (FermiML) framework is (i) versatile enough to encompass kernel methods and neural networks, (ii) applicable to classification and regression, and (iii) scalable to real-world datasets. FermiML models are quantum circuits sharing the building blocks of most quantum ML (QML) models: (parameterized) qubit rotations and entangling gates. This allows us to build fermionic surrogates that mimic the architecture, and hence the quantum resources and inductive bias, of any QML model while remaining efficiently classically simulable. We thus benchmark QML models against close fermionic counterparts on equal footing and ascertain whether a purported QML gain truly stems from classically inaccessible resources or is an accidental side-effect. Across 31 configurations from five classification datasets, we benchmark quantum kitchen sinks (QKS), instantaneous quantum polynomial (IQP) and generic parameterized quantum circuit (PQC) models against fermionic surrogates. fQKS significantly outperforms QKS and is statistically indistinguishable from IQP and PQC; fPQC outperforms IQP and QKS and ties PQC in 28 configurations. We also introduce fermionic fidelity and Pfaffian covariance kernels for regression and establish QML baselines for this harder task. Finally, we introduce a fermionic energy-based classifier scalable to large text and image datasets, which outperforms prominent QML models on images, beats or closely trails them on text, and stays close to classical baselines throughout. Our results show that while performance depends sensitively on architecture, FermiML yields fermionic surrogates that challenge or outperform their unrestricted counterparts and fermionic QML models that match the scale of classical baselines on real-world datasets.

title: Magnetoelectric response to a Néel domain wall in spin-orbit coupled superconducting films: Spontaneous currents, vortex pinning, and vortex-antivortex nucleation
summary: We study the superconducting response induced by a Néel domain wall in a thin superconducting film proximity-coupled to a ferromagnetic layer in the presence of interfacial Rashba spin-orbit coupling. The combined action of the magnetic texture and broken inversion symmetry generates a magnetoelectric coupling that induces spontaneous equilibrium currents. To establish the basic response to a continuously rotating magnetic texture, we first consider a periodic harmonic cycloid as an analytically tractable reference problem. Near Tc, this reference problem illustrates how the magnetoelectric coupling modifies the superconducting order parameter, while below Tc it provides a simple setting for describing the phase response, Pearl screening, and the interaction with a vortex. We then turn to the main problem of this work, a single Néel domain wall, and derive analytical expressions for its equilibrium phase profile, spontaneous current, magnetic field, and vortex-wall interaction energy.We show that the Néel wall acts as an extended magnetoelectric source and produces a vorticity-selective pinning landscape controlled by the competition between the wall width and the effective screening length. We further demonstrate that sufficiently strong magnetoelectric coupling can render a bound vortex-antivortex pair energetically favorable relative to the vortex-free state, even in the absence of an applied magnetic field. Our results provide an analytical framework for understanding magnetoelectric vortex pinning and vortex-antivortex nucleation by Néel domain walls in spin-orbit coupled superconducting films.

title: AI-assisted formal proofs for static and time-dependent density functional theory on lattices
summary: The Hohenberg-Kohn theorem fails on lattices, where two potentials that differ by more than a constant can share a ground state. We prove that such potentials are exceptional. We consider spinless fermions on any connected lattice, at any filling other than empty or full, with hopping amplitudes of a common sign and any density-density interaction. The potentials whose ground state is shared with a potential differing by more than a constant lie in a closed, nowhere dense set of zero Lebesgue measure. The densities of non-degenerate shared ground states form a set of codimension at least two. The statement about the potentials also holds for the Kohn-Sham potential and for spin-density functional theory, where a uniform shift of the magnetic field is the only additional freedom. In time-dependent density functional theory on lattices, we show that not every ground state of a connected lattice can serve as the initial state of the density-potential map. A counterexample is the ground state of two fermions on a square that Penz and van Leeuwen found as a counterexample to the Hohenberg-Kohn theorem. For almost every static potential, however, every real ground state can serve as an initial state, also for spin-resolved densities. We also give formal proofs that the time-dependent Kohn-Sham potential exists, locally in time, for almost every static Kohn-Sham potential, and of known results: local existence and uniqueness of the time-dependent potential for an admissible initial state, continuation in time up to the boundary of the set of admissible states, and the convergence properties of a regularized Kohn-Sham iteration. All theorems and propositions are formalized in the proof assistant Lean 4 and checked by computer.

title: The polarization bundle of a bending ray: nested projections and helicity Chern numbers
summary: We consider a ray propagating in a weakly anisotropic, possibly absorbing medium. The transverse planes of the propagation directions form a rank-two complex vector bundle $E_\perp$ over the sphere $S^2$ of directions. The polarization states are the points of $Z=\mathbb{CP}(E_\perp)$. Projecting the flat derivative of $\mathbb{C}^3$ onto $E_\perp$ gives a connection $D$, the complexified Levi-Civita connection of $S^2$, whose holonomy is the Rytov rotation. Projecting $D$ onto a polarization line gives the connection of the tautological line bundle over $Z$, whose holonomy is the Pancharatnam--Berry phase. For the horizontal distribution defined by $D$, the curvature of this bundle is $iω_{\mathrm{FS}}$ on the vertical part, $i s_3\,ω$ on the horizontal part, and zero on the mixed part. Here $ω_{\mathrm{FS}}$ is the Fubini--Study form, $ω$ the area form of $S^2$, and $s_3$ the circular Stokes parameter. The Rytov rotation, the Pancharatnam--Berry phase and the Chern numbers $c_1(L_\pm)=\mp 2$ are all obtained from this curvature. Restricted to the helicity sections, it gives the obstruction to a globally smooth circular Jones vector, although the circular polarization states are globally defined.

title: Spinal reflected entropy reveals logical magic
summary: Entanglement and magic are usually regarded as independent quantum resources. Here we connect the two in the toric code, where the stabilizer Rényi entropy of the stored logical state, a widely used measure of magic, acquires a direct interpretation in terms of entanglement. We introduce the spinal reflected entropy, defined on a neighborhood of a spine of the underlying surface as the reflected entropy between a disk around the vertex of the spine and bands along its noncontractible loops. It obeys an area law with a topological correction and contains one additional term that carries all the dependence on the stored state. On a torus, this term equals the stabilizer Rényi entropy of the stored state plus the logarithm of the ground-state degeneracy. The mechanism is topological. On the surface sewn to its reflected copy, the bands close into tubes, logical Pauli operators become anyon charges threading them, and these charges are distributed as the outcomes of Bell sampling of the stored state. The result extends to surfaces of higher genus and to general two-dimensional topological stabilizer codes on qubits. Logical magic thus becomes a geometrically defined entanglement quantity, one that shallow circuits preserving the code space cannot change.

title: Towards determination of intrinsic spin properties in MAPbI$_3$ crystals using spin noise spectroscopy
summary: Spin noise spectroscopy in back- and forward-scattering geometries is used to study the spin dynamics of charge carriers in a MAPbI$_3$ (MA = methylammonium) single crystal. The spectra reveal electrons and holes with different degrees of localization. At low temperatures ($T \approx 4$~K), hole spin relaxation is dominated by the hyperfine interaction with nuclear spins. The broadening of the spectra with increasing temperature can be attributed to thermally activated hopping of localized holes. From the thermal activation energies, we estimate hole localization lengths that are consistent with both the hyperfine-induced dephasing rates and the zero-field frequency shifts measured at low temperature. By contrast, the electron spin dynamics cannot be explained by the hyperfine interaction alone: even at the lowest excitation powers, it is affected by the probe light, and we observe a slowing down of spin relaxation with increasing power. Comparison of the back- and forward-scattered spin noise signals indicates that the spatial distribution of carriers is inhomogeneous: electrons are located preferentially near the crystal surface, weakly localized holes (characterized by slower spin relaxation) are found mostly away from the surface, and strongly localized holes are somewhere in between.

title: Probing the inner structure of bound states
summary: We show how constructing a composite particle eigenstate reveals its internal structure. Using quantum subspace expansion (QSE), we optimize states with different sets of operators and use their fidelities with the full QSE state to measure the importance of each added operator type. Taking the scalar meson of the massive Schwinger model as a benchmark, we find that fermion bilinears suffice at large fermion masses. At small masses, two classes of four-fermion operators play important but very different roles: the four fermion operators with two fermions and 2 anti-fermions at small distance give little improvement. In contrast, spatially extended meson-meson operators produce a large gain in state fidelity. Turning to observables, we find that the scalar charge is much more sensitive to the meson-meson operators than e.g. the meson mass. The parton distribution function (PDF) also changes from symmetric to asymmetric about the momentum fraction 1/2, along with the growing importance of meson-meson operators. These results establish QSE as a tool for probing the internal structure of composite particles and connecting it to observable properties.

title: Exact Response Theory based on Karhunen-Loève Expansions for Brownian Oscillators
summary: We extend Exact Response Theory (ERT) to an overdamped Brownian oscillator driven by thermal white noise. The stochastic forcing is represented by a Karhunen--Loève series and embedded into an autonomous, augmented phase space using a harmonic auxiliary phase. This representation allows us to construct the ERT dissipation function for fixed mode amplitudes and recover stochastic averages by averaging over the amplitudes and the initial phase. For the variance, we derive the response at finite spectral truncation and show analytically that, with uniform phase sampling, the full-spectrum white-noise limit reproduces the generator-based result for a sudden temperature change. Furthermore, a comparison with first-order linear response theory highlights how this may fail in general. In particular, if the noise-induced variance is quadratic in the noise amplitude, it is completely omitted by linear response. The analysis provides a framework for this model and for studying more general forcing; extensions to non-Markovian dynamics require separate convergence and regularity analyses.

title: Strong Co-O exchange interaction in $P4/nmm$ KCoO$_2$ and its effect on spin wave and Néel temperature
summary:
The exchange interactions of a classical Heisenberg Hamiltonian
  in KCoO$_2$ in the $P4/nnm$ structure
  are calculated using a linear response approach, derived from the transverse
  spin susceptibility, integrated over atomic spheres using a projector proportional the local magnetization and including all atoms as magnetic atoms. The exchange interaction between Co and its apical O is found to be by far the largest interaction and ferromagnetic. Its effect on the Néel temperature and the spin wave spectrum are evaluated. The Co-O exchange is found to strongly enhance the critical temperature in the mean field approximation but not in the random phase approximation.

title: From Fermions to Vortices: Microscopic Simulations of Phase Ordering in a d-Wave Superconductor
summary: Describing bath-induced superconducting phase ordering directly from a microscopic fermionic Hamiltonian remains a formidable challenge. Here we develop a microscopic framework for this problem using the recently introduced adiabatic variational principle (AVP) and demonstrate its application to a two-dimensional $d$-wave superconductor. The central construction maps evolving, spatially inhomogeneous bond-pairing fields onto constrained Bogoliubov-de Gennes states, with the associated Lagrange multipliers determining the thermodynamic driving forces. This enables dissipative evolution of the superconducting order while retaining its microscopic electronic structure, without assuming a phenomenological Ginzburg-Landau free-energy functional. Starting from disordered pairing configurations, we resolve the emergence of phase coherence through vortex-antivortex annihilation and the accompanying evolution of local electronic spectra. Vortex decay and dynamical scaling recover the characteristic kinetics of two-dimensional phase ordering, providing a nontrivial benchmark of the framework. The solver-independent AVP formulation opens a route to microscopic studies of dissipative ordering and metastability in superconductors with intertwined stripe and pair-density-wave orders.

title: Continuum model for disconnection structures of hetero-interfaces
summary: Hetero-interfaces, as planar defects between dissimilar materials, accommodate the lattice misfit through networks of line defects of disconnections (a combination of structural ledges/step and dislocation characters).
