We develop a continuum model that predicts the hetero-interface structures, including disconnection networks, the interface inclination and misorientation angles. The model is based on the interfacial energy minimization with respect to all possible disconnection modes, subject to the interface structure constraint of the generalized Frank-Bilby equation that describes the lattice correspondence across the interface including both dislocation and step characters of disconnections and the inclination and misorientation angles. Numerical simulations are performed to determine the equilibrium configurations of three different types of hetero-interfaces: the $α$/$β$ (orthorhombic/monoclinic) interface in ZrO$_2$, $α$/$β$ hetero-interfaces in Ti and Au/Pd (001) twist-misfit interfaces. Comparisons with experiments, atomistic simulations and theoretical predictions show that our continuum model provides excellent predictions of the hetero-interface structures including disconnection networks and inclination, misorientation angles. Furthermore, systematic analysis reveals the functional dependence of hetero-interface structural properties on inclination and misorientation angles.

title: Compressional-shear wave interference and wave suppression at exceptional-point gaps
summary: Exceptional points (EPs) in complex elastic materials signify the coalescence of compressional and shear modes and bound a frequency gap where waves become evanescent. While their effects on wave propagation have been extensively studied, the physical mechanisms underlying their existence remain elusive. In this Letter, employing a transfer matrix formulation combined with Bloch's theorem, we demonstrate that the gaps bounded by EPs in layered media originate from destructive interference between the compressional and shear wave fields. We further reveal that the corresponding wavenumbers satisfy a Bragg-like condition with the unit cell thickness, causing the total wave field to become stationary, forming a standing wave. Finally, a finite layered medium is considered, where this mechanism is shown to manifest as forbidden wave propagation for both modes in the gap. These results provide a direct physical interpretation of EPs.

title: Quantum State Preparation from Nonreversible Markov Chains via Spectral Filtering
summary: We develop a framework for preparing and transporting coherent quantum samples of nonreversible Markov chains. Our approach uses spectral filtering to construct state-dependent phase operations, which are combined with fixed-point amplitude amplification to transport quantum states along a sequence of related chains. We study two complementary constructions with different oracle requirements and target states. The first uses coherent access to both forward and time-reversed transitions and targets the stationary quantum sample, with a filtering cost governed by a multiplicative-reversibilization gap. The second requires only forward transitions and selects the leading eigenstate of a flat discriminant, which may differ from the stationary quantum sample; we quantify this bias under additional spectral and reversibility-on-average conditions. For the forward-only construction, we implement the spectral filter using generalized quantum signal processing with a single signal qubit, apart from transition registers and oracle workspace. We establish a common transport procedure and derive error and resource bounds that account for spectral properties, overlaps between successive selected states, and the costs of coherent multi-step transition oracles. Up to logarithmic factors, spectral-filter degrees scale inversely with the square roots of the relevant spectral gaps, while transport introduces an additional inverse-square-root dependence on certified lower bounds on squared overlaps between successive selected states. Our results extend existing nonreversible spectral methods to multistage coherent state transport with controlled approximation errors.

title: Topological Narrow Bands in Twisted Rhombohedral Multilayer Graphene
comment: 14 pages, 6 figures, plus Supplemental Material (17 pages, 13 figures)
summary: Moiré graphene multilayers provide an atomically thin platform for engineering narrow topological bands through stacking, twist, and electrostatic control. Recent experiments on twisted rhombohedral graphene have revealed a high-Chern-number hierarchy determined by the number of rhombohedral layers. A microscopic description of this hierarchy requires connecting the ideal chiral picture to the realistic electronic structure. Here, we show that the two central moiré bands of twisted monolayer-$N$-layer rhombohedral graphene originate from hybridization between a monolayer Dirac cone and a rhombohedral surface state located at opposite corners of the moiré Brillouin zone. Increasing $N$ progressively narrows these bands, whereas reversing the displacement field transfers their wave-function weight between the twisted interface and the remote surface. In spectrally isolated regimes, this redistribution switches the lower band between Chern numbers $\mathcal{C}=N$ and $\mathcal{C}=-1$. A projected surface theory shows how interfacial tunneling is dressed by virtual propagation through the rhombohedral stack, explaining the field-selected Chern hierarchy and the recurring threefold structure of the real-space charge textures. These results establish layer number and displacement field as complementary nanoscale controls of band flatness, spatial polarization, and topology in graphene moiré heterostructures.

title: Space-Time Point Defects as Probes of Criticality: Application to the Gross-Neveu-Heisenberg Transition
summary: At criticality, a local field acting at a single point in Euclidean space-time is irrelevant and induces a modulation in space and time that decays with twice its scaling dimension. This turns two-point correlation functions into one-point measurements: one operator insertion enters the Boltzmann weight, the other is measured. For the local magnetization the relation is exact at any source strength. Implemented in auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo, the approach yields the static spin susceptibility and imaginary-time-displaced correlations with unprecedented precision. We apply it to the Dirac-semimetal to antiferromagnetic-Mott-insulator transition of the half-filled $π$-flux Hubbard model. This lattice model provides a regularization of the $N_f=2$ Gross-Neveu-Heisenberg universality class. A finite-size scaling analysis estimates the critical exponents as $ ν=1.10(3)$ and $η_φ=1.09(4)$, close to field-theory predictions of $η_φ\simeq1$. Since $η_φ>1$, the equal-time structure factor at criticality does not diverge with the system size. Hence, the equal-time structure factor at the ordering wave vector is dominated by background contributions and cannot be used for extracting critical exponents. Consistently, the spin dynamics at the transition is strongly incoherent and the quantum Fisher information remains bounded.

title: Network topology imposes spectral constraints on collective nonequilibrium responses
comment: 17 pages and 4 figures in the main text; 10 pages and 11 figures in the Supplemental Material
summary: Collective nonequilibrium dynamics in Langevin systems depend on both network topology and stochastic driving. Understanding the role of topology in responses to stochastic driving and in the emergence of nonequilibrium is essential. Starting from the principle of microscopic reversibility and linear Langevin dynamics on networks, we derive a mode decomposition for both the asymmetry of short-time cross-correlations and heat currents at steady state. This decomposition reveals two sources of nonequilibrium---fluctuations of individual modes and correlated fluctuations between distinct modes. For reciprocal networks with independent local driving, we derive two nonequilibrium response operators that yield explicit expressions for the global asymmetry intensity and the entropy production rate. These operators are weighted Laplacians independent of stochastic driving. Their spectra determine attainable upper and lower bounds on nonequilibrium at fixed driving heterogeneity. These bounds are exact for asymmetry intensity at arbitrary deviations from equilibrium and hold to leading order near equilibrium for entropy production rate. Finally, we find that the hierarchical modular organization of human structural connectomes broadens the brain's nonequilibrium operating range, with resting-state brain activity supporting this topological advantage for sustaining a lower nonequilibrium level. Our study provides a basis for understanding biological network organization and designing networks with targeted nonequilibrium operating points.

title: Spin Hamiltonian, magnetic anisotropy and excitation spectrum in altermagnetic $α$-MnTe from first principles
summary: The hexagonal altermagnet $α$-MnTe combines a near-room-temperature collinear order with a strongly spin-split electronic structure, yet the microscopic origin of its easy-plane anisotropy, its zone-center magnon gap and its anomalously large magnetostriction have remained unexplained. We derive the complete low-energy magnetic Hamiltonian of $α$-MnTe from first principles, combining density functional theory and dynamical mean-field theory with a force-theorem evaluation of the full anisotropic intersite exchange, single-ion terms and classical dipolar couplings. The isotropic exchange, including the altermagnetic splitting of the tenth-neighbor coupling, agrees with inelastic neutron scattering data. Contrary to the common single-ion picture, we find that the easy-plane anisotropy and the magnon gap at $Γ$ are governed by classical dipole-dipole interactions, which enhance the zone-center magnon splitting threefold leading to quantitative agreement with experiment, while the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya term is irrelevant despite its size. The same Hamiltonian reproduces the chiral magnon splitting along antinodal directions, mirroring the electronic spin splitting, and quantitatively accounts for the giant magnetovolume coupling of $α$-MnTe through the volume dependence of superexchange.

title: Topological Anderson Superconductor in Landau Levels
summary: There is much interest in two-dimensional superconductors with odd integer values of the Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) Chern number $C_{\rm BdG}$, often termed topological superconductors, as these are predicted to harbor Majorana zero modes. Because a magnetic field produces Landau levels (LL) with nonzero Chern numbers, it is natural to ask if a conventional two-dimensional superconductor of spinful fermions with Rashba spin-orbit coupling can be driven topological by application of a magnetic field. Self-consistent solutions of the BdG equations for an on-site attractive interaction produce a phase diagram consisting almost everywhere of superconducting states with even integer values of $C_{\rm BdG}$, transitioning from one value to another as parameters such as the chemical potential are varied. We predict that introducing Anderson-type on-site disorder, which broadens as well as mixes LLs, produces, in the transition region, states wherein topological superconductivity percolates. This topological Anderson superconducting state provides another example where disorder can produce topologically nontrivial states.

title: Thermodynamics of complex crystals from a generalized mean-field bond model
comment: 16 pages, 8 figures, 2 tables. Code: https://github.com/raynol-dsouza/mean-field-bond-model (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24493341). Data: doi:10.5281/zenodo.24466123
summary: We extend our previously introduced mean-field bond model from unary fcc lattices to crystals with multiple chemical species and sublattices, accurately predicting finite-temperature thermodynamics without statistical sampling. Our generalization reformulates the model in terms of the Wyckoff positions of the crystal, representing each by one atom, and solving for the bond density of the reference bond of each of its neighbor shells. Bond-bond correlation functions are built from the zero-temperature force constants, allowing the deviation of every bond in the crystal to be expressed through linear functions of the reference bond of a shell. Thermodynamic self-consistency is enforced by requiring a single virial temperature for the whole crystal, and compatibility of average bond lengths with crystal volume. Model predictions are validated against molecular dynamics simulations of unary, binary, and ternary crystals using Morse-type bonding potentials, parametrized for each shell from the force constants of empirical interatomic potentials at several isotropic strains. In each case, the predicted bond densities and thermodynamics agree with the simulations to within their statistical uncertainty. We discuss strategies for combining the model with bonding potentials parametrized from first principles and foundation models to predict the finite-temperature thermodynamics of complex crystals at ab initio accuracy without statistical sampling.

title: Correlation functions of 2D critical models via a KPZ relation for conformal blocks
comment: 7 pages, 2 figures. This Letter is aimed at physicists and mathematicians who are primarily interested in the global picture. Full mathematical details will be presented in a forthcoming paper
summary: The Knizhnik--Polyakov--Zamolodchikov (KPZ) relation allows scaling exponents of two-dimensional (2D) critical systems to be derived from their counterparts in Liouville quantum gravity. We extend this framework to correlation functions based on an integral inversion relation between Virasoro conformal blocks with complementary central charges $c$ and $26-c$. We demonstrate this method in various models by deriving the 2-point disk correlation from their quantum counterpart and the KPZ relation. Results on critical loop models were previously known, but our method is robust enough to include many scenarios previously unsolved, such as the Fuzzy Potts model. Our approach is complementary to the conformal bootstrap.

title: A Constraint-Preserving Preconditioned Quantum Solver for Heterogeneous Brinkman Flo
summary: Quantum amplitude estimation can reduce the number of evaluations needed to estimate an average, but its advantage in PDE uncertainty quantification depends on the cost of each coherent solve. We study this problem for incompressible Brinkman flow through a porous material with spatially varying drag. We first express the velocity in divergence-free coordinates using a polar Riesz map, obtaining a positive-definite system that preserves incompressibility in the exact formulation. We then introduce a Sobolev--Riesz preconditioner and prove that the resulting condition number is bounded by $α_{\max}/α_{\min}$, independently of the grid resolution. We construct block encodings and reversible-arithmetic circuits for this formulation and show how to estimate the mean kinetic energy without reconstructing the full velocity field. By accounting for both sampling and solver costs, we establish conditions under which the method has a gate-complexity advantage over single-level classical grid-resolving solvers. Numerical experiments verify the conditioning bound and the accuracy of the circuit components at the tested sizes. The complexity advantage is conditional on the stated input and discretization assumptions; no quantum-hardware runtime advantage is demonstrated.

title: Periodic and quasiperiodic structures produced by microphase separation in one-component simple liquids with competing interactions
summary: Competing interactions can generate frustration which suppresses macroscopic-scale phase separation, superseding it with separation patterns on the microscopic scale. This phenomenon, referred to as microphase separation, produces thermodynamically stable mesoscopic-scale periodic patterns in systems of different physical nature. The studies of this effect follow two paradigms. First, in block copolymers, the macroscopic-scale separation of chemically distinct components is prevented by the covalent bonds between them. In the other, the microscopic-scale separation is produced in simple single-component liquids by the competition between a short-range attraction and a long-range repulsion (SALR) in the pair potential, the separation occurring between a dense phase and a gas. The interest in the simple liquid models with SALR interaction was inspired by the apparent universality of the modulated structures generated by competing interactions in different systems. Simple particle models are tractable by theory and thereby make it possible to discern the microscopic mechanisms of pattern formation; particle-based simulations give access to systems beyond the reach of experiments. In this Perspective we review the recent advances in the molecular-dynamics simulation of microphase separation in single-component simple liquids using SALR potentials. We show that these simulations reproduce the mesophases typical of block copolymers and liquid crystals, which demonstrates that the complexity of the constituent particles of real liquids is not a necessary condition for their formation, and that they produce novel periodic morphologies of both conceptual interest and technological relevance; we discuss how simulated mesophases can serve as templates for metamaterials whose properties are governed by topology.

title: Dynamic scaling behaviors induced by periodic drivings at continuous Ising quantum transitions
summary: We investigate the out-of-equilibrium scaling behaviors induced by periodic driving protocols in quantum many-body systems near continuous quantum phase transitions at zero temperature. We consider two paradigmatic one-dimensional systems: the quantum Ising chain subject to periodic longitudinal fields and the Kitaev fermionic wire with periodically driven chemical potentials, equivalent to a quantum Ising chain with a periodic transverse field. Within a renormalization-group (RG) framework, we develop a dynamic scaling theory for both finite-size systems and the thermodynamic limit, identifying scaling variables associated with the driving amplitude and period. We distinguish between protocols that break the global ${\mathbb Z}_2$ symmetry by coupling to the order parameter and those that preserve it. These two classes of driving exhibit distinct scaling behaviors, with power-law exponents determined by the RG dimensions of the corresponding perturbations. We verify the proposed dynamic scaling theory through numerical simulations of both smooth single-frequency and discontinuous square-wave periodic drivings.

title: Adaptive ghost Gutzwiller dynamics of Hubbard model quenches across coupling strengths over extended times
summary: Following the real-time dynamics of correlated electrons to extended times, at all interaction strengths, remains an open challenge. We address it with an adaptive time-dependent ghost Gutzwiller approximation (td-gGA). The method extends the Gutzwiller approximation by auxiliary ghost orbitals. It adds more of them whenever the correlations that build up during the dynamics exceed a threshold. This is computationally far more efficient than keeping their number fixed. As a demonstration we take the interaction quench of the half-filled Hubbard model on the Bethe lattice. For this paradigmatic problem, numerically exact nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) serves as the reference. A previous td-gGA study with a fixed set of 6 ghost orbitals per spin largely reproduced the available DMFT data. It lacked, however, an error estimate that would support predictions beyond them. With up to 16 ghost orbitals per spin, adaptive td-gGA agrees with DMFT wherever DMFT data are available, from the weak-coupling prethermal regime to the strong-coupling collapse-and-revival regime. At strong coupling it remains converged up to three and a half times as long as the DMFT data. Near the crossover between the two regimes, the system relaxes to thermal values that agree with DMFT. Resolving the dynamics in the number of ghost orbitals shows how the sharp dynamical transition of the Gutzwiller approximation turns into this smooth crossover. In the extended time window at strong coupling, we observe that the oscillation frequency is renormalized as predicted by our second-order strong-coupling expansion. With its built-in error estimate, adaptive td-gGA offers a systematically improvable route to the extended-time dynamics of driven and multi-orbital correlated systems, especially when combined with tensor-network or quantum solvers for the embedding problem.

title: Multistable Thermoelectric Josephson Automata
summary: Multistable systems can store and process information, yet their elements usually only burn the drive energy. Here, we build an automaton whose elements actively convert heat into electrical power. Heat alone stabilizes the states at zero bias, and each state routes generation and dissipation to different junctions. The elements, gap-asymmetric superconducting tunnel junctions, deliver up to 2.6 pW at either polarity under fixed heating and support a magnetic-field-tunable Josephson current. Two junctions sharing a heated island split the bias hysteretically and, even at zero bias, lock into opposite voltages encoding the sweep direction. With a load and current bias, the automaton accesses states spanning junction polarity combinations, including zero voltage; the magnetic field sets which are available and the bias history selects the occupied one.

title: Spin-Group versus Magnetic-Group Selection Rules for Nonlinear Photocurrents in Compensated Ferrimagnets
summary: Optical excitation offers a contact-free, ultrafast route to charge and spin currents, with symmetry determining which nonlinear photocurrents are allowed and whether they carry charge, spin, or both. Spin-group symmetry describes the limit without spin-orbit coupling (SOC), whereas magnetic-group symmetry accounts for SOC. We show that the two descriptions yield different selection rules for both charge and spin photocurrents in the multiferroic compensated ferrimagnet GaFeO$_3$. Without SOC, only linear shift and circular injection currents are allowed, with identical components for charge and spin, so every charge current is spin polarized along the moments. SOC leaves these charge currents nearly unchanged, activates magnetic linear injection and circular shift charge currents, and enables pure spin currents polarized perpendicular to the moments. Ferroelectric switching reverses the linear shift and circular injection charge currents and their spin polarization. These findings establish the importance of magnetic-group symmetry for a complete description of nonlinear charge and spin photocurrents in compensated ferrimagnets.

title: On Lipschitz equicontinuity of random Schrödinger operators on lattices
summary: We consider random Schrödinger operators on $\mathbb{Z}^d$. We prove that the density of states is uniformly bounded in the coupling strength for a dense set of single site probability distributions.

title: Quantum Control Under Control-Dependent Decoherence
summary: Decoherence, which arises from the interaction of a quantum system with a typically much larger thermal environment, or bath, poses major challenges to the controllability of quantum systems. The dynamics of such open quantum systems is often represented by Markovian quantum master equations of the Lindblad or Redfield type. These equations describe the dynamics of the open system with a sum of coherent (Hamiltonian) and decoherent (dissipative) contributions. It is often assumed that coherent controls only impact the coherent contribution, while the decoherent contribution is taken to be time- and control-independent. However, the decoherent contribution must also be control-dependent if coupling to a thermal bath is to relax the system to a Gibbs state at thermal equilibrium, which is given in terms of the system's Hamiltonian. In this paper, we investigate the effect of accounting for control-dependent decoherence on coherent control protocols. To this end, we examine the effect of accounting for control-dependent decoherence on the controllability of an open quantum system in the case of a two-level system coupled to a thermal bath. We show that coherent controls wield greater influence on the dynamics of the system than predicted by a Lindblad-type equation that models decoherence as time- and control-independent.

title: Angular Momentum Hall Effect of Axial Ferrons in Ferroelectrics
summary: Phonon thermal and angular-momentum (AM) Hall effects are known in non-ferroelectric insulators, yet whether terahertz soft modes of displacive ferroelectrics, i.e., ``ferrons", share them remains open. We report axial ferrons that hold polarization-momentum locking in uniaxial ferroelectrics and show that both effects exist: a longitudinal temperature gradient drives a transverse AM flow without any field, whereas an out-of-plane magnetic field switches on the thermal Hall response. Two competitive channels emerge for the AM Hall effect: self-radiated magnetic fields hybridize two branches into circular modes whose momentum-locked Berry curvature deflects opposite magnetic moments to opposite edges, while temperature-gradient-induced mode quantum coherence adds a magnetic-moment dipole that leads to an opposite transverse AM current. An out-of-plane magnetic field breaks the exact polarization-momentum locking and yields a polarization Hall current. Numerical calculations show these effects are significant in both LiNbO$_3$ and van der Waals ferroelectrics. Edge magnetization or polarization accumulation can switch adjacent magnets or ferroelectrics, enabling low-power magnetoelectric functionality by thermal current in the future.

title: Classifying exact local-equilibrium solutions of the Boltzmann equation
summary: We provide a complete classification, in a \(d\)-dimensional Euclidean space, of all hydrodynamic states and external forces for which a local equilibrium distribution constitutes an exact solution to the Boltzmann kinetic equation. We demonstrate that the temperature \(T\) must be spatially uniform, that the velocity field is the sum of a rigid translation, a radial expansion or compression, and a rigid rotation, and that the external acceleration must be conservative, though time-dependent within a reference frame that translates and rotates along with the fluid. The density profile is then determined by the external potential, while its temporal dependence is governed by any temperature function \(T(t)\) that can be generated through an appropriate adjustment of the external acceleration. We recover the classic ``harmonic breather'' and obtain solutions involving static forces that exhibit algebraic cooling, similar to Haff's law, despite the occurrence of elastic collisions. Our classification identifies the exceptional circumstances under which local equilibrium is exact and provides rigorous criteria for evaluating kinetic and hydrodynamic approximations.

title: Universal spectrum of weakly coupled quantum critical Ising chains
summary: We study the spectrum of arrays of critical transverse field Ising chains perturbed by a weak inter-chain coupling in the scaling limit, using an exact diagonalization algorithm based on Hamiltonian truncation. As the number of chains is made large, we confirm the existence of excitations below the two particle continuum that can be identified with the celebrated Zamalodchikov $E_8$ theory with small corrections. In addition, we find a distinct $ψ$-particle, with mass $M_\mathrmψ$ which is not contained in the $E_8$ theory. Its ratio to the lowest $E_8$ mass ($M_1$) is a universal number, which we have computed numerically to be $M_\mathrmψ/M_1 = 1.819\cdots$ for a one dimensional array of critical chains. We present evidence that this new state fundamentally involves excitations on neighboring chains, explaining why it has no analogue in the single chain problem. Interestingly the $M_\mathrmψ$ mass has a characteristic scaling dependence on detuning from the critical point that is qualitatively distinct from the $E_8$ masses, which can help identify it in spectroscopic experiments on easy-axis magnetic chain materials.

title: Constrained Allen-Cahn phase-field topology optimization of flexoelectric devices
summary: Topology optimization provides an effective approach to exploring performance-oriented designs for miniature devices. In this work, a phase-field framework for constrained topology optimization of microscale flexoelectric devices is developed using a continuum model under the assumption of infinitesimal deformations. The material distribution is optimized at the device level with the output voltage as the objective. The framework also accommodates objectives based on capacitance or stored electrostatic energy. Manufacturing variations are incorporated through a worst-case objective over the prescribed geometric realizations, with spectral constraints imposed to maintain the structural connectivity. The framework is applied to two-dimensional pressure and bending sensors and a three-dimensional thin-film device. The optimized nominal output voltages reach approximately 4.8 times the initial value for the pressure sensor and 2.5-3.4 times the initial values for the bending sensors. The voltage gains arise primarily from increased mechanically induced source charge, with capacitance reduction providing an additional contribution that varies with the device configuration. Erosion analyses of representative designs further show that structural connectivity is well preserved when structural members become locally narrower, with the output voltage remaining close to that of the nominal configuration. Combined with specific microfabrication processes, this optimization framework is expected to provide a numerical basis for configuration screening and prototype development of flexoelectric devices.

title: Krylov dynamics of deformed oscillator chains: localization, ballistic spreading, and indeterminacy
summary: Krylov and spread complexity map quantum dynamics onto a quantum walk on a half-line whose hopping amplitudes are the Lanczos coefficients, so that Krylov dynamics is the theory of orthogonal polynomials and Jacobi operators. We use this correspondence to study Krylov chains generated by the two-parameter $(p,q)$-deformed oscillator, which interpolates between the Heisenberg--Weyl chain, the $q$-oscillator chain of double-scaled SYK, and chains with exponentially growing Lanczos coefficients. For the deformed displacement chain the spread complexity is the mean excitation number, its rate is the deformed momentum quadrature, and its acceleration is $\ddot C_K=2ω^2\langle[a,a^\dagger]\rangle$, so the deformed commutator acts as a force along the Krylov chain and the mean deformation controls early-time growth. The deformation parameters separate four regimes. For $\max(p,q)<1$ the complexity stays bounded, a localization produced by the algebra alone. For $p=1$, $q<1$ it grows ballistically, with an exact asymptotic velocity given by a theta-type series. At $p=q=1$ it grows as $t^2$. For $\max(p,q)>1$ the Jacobi operator is not essentially self-adjoint, the moment problem is indeterminate, and the Lanczos coefficients no longer determine the dynamics. Even and odd truncations converge to two different evolutions, the two reflection-symmetric N-extremal solutions of the moment problem, the odd one carrying a zero-energy atom of closed-form weight; the self-adjoint extensions yield a family of complexity curves that coincide at early times and separate once the Krylov wavefront reaches infinity. Krylov complexity in this regime is thus defined only once a boundary condition at infinite Krylov index is specified. The orthogonal-polynomial procedure and its checks on exactly solvable chains are given in the appendices.

title: Long-range effective interactions in a rectangular tight-binding lattice within the semiclassical approximation
summary: We extend the semiclassical formalism of Dunlap--Kenkre (1986) and of Mamani et al. (2017) to obtain the effective Hamiltonian of a rectangular tight-binding lattice with interactions to all neighbors, in the presence of a rapidly oscillating field $\mathbf f(ωt)$ and a static potential $V(x,y)$, both arbitrary, by means of: a canonical transformation, the semiclassical approximation and the Kapitza-type time-averaging techniques (Mamani 2017). At zeroth order in $1/ω$, a field with even symmetry reparameterizes the hopping elements through factors in terms of Bessel functions. At order $1/ω^2$, the induced hopping elements arise from the coupling between the oscillating field and the curvature of the static potential (its 2nd derivative). For fields $\mathbf f(ωt)$ with odd symmetry, in addition to renormalizing the interactions, an effective band shift appears. For the two-dimensional lattice, we obtain the generalization of the exact dynamic localization condition of Dignam et al. (2002) and Domachuk et al. (2002), and we show that the resulting band-collapse is in general anisotropic --axial interactions are suppressed but some diagonal interactions persist--, so that exact dynamic localization in the stroboscopic sense is guaranteed only when the band-collapse is complete for all neighbors. Finally, we numerically identify an effective-duplication scenario for the rectangular lattice, associated with approximate solutions of a Pythagorean-type relation among zeros of the zeroth-order Bessel function.

title: Reconfigurable Chiral Phonons and Their Selection in Asymmetrically Stacked Graphene MoirMoiré Superlattices
summary: Chiral phonons, lattice vibrations carrying angular momentum, offer a new handle for controlling phonon-mediated phenomena in condensed matter, yet their on-demand generation and deterministic control remain challenging. Here we show, using helicity-resolved Raman spectroscopy, that asymmetrically stacked graphene moiré superlattices provide a reconfigurable platform for chiral phonons. We observe a finite degree of circular polarization for both chiral interlayer shear phonons and intralayer optical phonons. A chiral-phonon Raman-tensor model attributes this response to interfacial $C_{2}$-symmetry breaking together with Raman resonance within the van Hove singularity region. Reversing either the twist sense or the stacking order inverts the degree of circular polarization through the spatial transformations linking the corresponding stacking geometries. By tuning the excitation energy and twist angle, we achieve nearly full-range control of the degree of circular polarization of interlayer shear phonons, from $-1$ to $1$, while gate-induced interlayer potential redistribution enables substantial and reversible in situ modulation. These results establish asymmetrically stacked graphene moiré superlattices as a versatile platform for generating and controlling chiral phonons, with implications for optoelectronic and quantum technologies.

title: On fluctuation properties of the cumulative current in gTASEP on open chains
summary: We present preliminary results of our numerical study of the fluctuation properties of the cumulative current, JT, in the generalized totally asymmetric simple exclusion process (gTASEP) on open chains with Liggett boundary conditions. GTASEP is the ordinary TASEP (a model of 1D- traffic on a single track, having many diverse applications), where an additional term controlling clustering of the particles is added. Extensive numerical simulations are performed to determine the dependence of the second scaled cumulant C2 of the time integrated current, JT, on the system size, L, in the long-time limit, allowing for comparison between open and periodic geometries. Preliminary results for C2 in the maximum current phase show agreement with theoretical predictions about the Kardar-Parizi-Zhang universality of the gTASEP on a segment.

title: Symmetry-dependent field-induced elastic renormalization in the quantum-critical medium-entropy alloy NiCoCr$_{0.8}$
summary: We investigate the elastic response of cubic NiCoCr$_{0.8}$, a quantum-critical medium-entropy alloy, by high-precision ultrasound velocity measurements. At zero magnetic field, the three symmetrically independent elastic moduli $C_{11}$, $(C_{11}-C_{12})/2=C_t$, and $C_{44}$ monotonically harden upon cooling without pronounced elastic softening or anomalies. In magnetic fields applied along [110], however, a minute but systematic elastic renormalization of the order of $10^{-5}$ is resolved at low temperatures. The tetragonal $E_g$ mode $C_t$ softens with increasing field, whereas the derived bulk $A_{1g}$ mode $C_B$ hardens, revealing an opposite field response between the two strain-symmetry channels. Comparison with the previously reported quantum-critical-Fermi-liquid crossover scale shows that the field-induced elastic renormalization develops already in the quantum-critical regime and evolves continuously across the crossover region, without a sharp elastic anomaly or threshold behavior. These results demonstrate that symmetry-resolved ultrasound provides a sensitive probe of subtle strain-dependent changes in the electronic and magnetic free energy of a chemically disordered itinerant quantum-critical metal.

title: Comparative Molecular Dynamics Study of Initial Oxide Film Growth on Al, Mg, and Ti Using a Universal Neural Network Potential
summary: Spontaneous formation of an oxide film, which may be passive, is found in many metals such as Al and Ti. We report direct computational observation of oxide film formation on the three major light structural metals, Al, Mg, and Ti, with molecular dynamics (MD) using a universal neural network potential (NNP). O2 molecules were supplied during MD simulations to replenish O consumed by the metal. Al and Ti formed a 1-2 nm thick film within a few ps of the simulation with O2 gas pressure of 102-103 atm. The film thicknesses of all metal oxides continued to increase proportionally to the logarithm of simulation time, consistent with Cabrera-Mott theory. Al and Ti oxides grow at the surface, while Mg oxide grows into the Mg metal. Al, Mg, and Ti are approximately 4.4, 4.3, and 5.2-fold coordinated, respectively, in the oxide.

title: Blueprint for DOE Quantum Supercomputing
comment: Prepared for the U.S. Department of Energy. Significant contributions are acknowledged from Brian Austin, Andrew Baczewski, Christian Bauer, Thomas Beck, Tanmoy Bhattacharya, Daan Camps, Zohreh Davoudi, Al Geist, Natalie Klco, Katie Klymko, Hank Lamm, Thomas Maier, Mason Rhodes, and Martin Savage
summary: Quantum computing stands at the threshold of a transformative decade, where the field will evolve from small-scale demonstrations toward practical scientific computing at scale. This Blueprint identifies fault-tolerant quantum computers (FTQCs) as a viable, scalable, and broadly applicable path to achieving "quantum scientific utility." It outlines a strategy to prepare the US Department of Energy (DOE) for FTQCs and their integration into the US national scientific computing infrastructure. Its purpose is to identify the steps, milestones, and research directions necessary for DOE to enable initial deployment of FTQCs in 2028 as a scientific tool for the nation and mature this capability into the 2030s. Given recent demonstrations of logical operations on error-corrected logical qubits and the advancement of commercial hardware roadmaps, DOE should begin preparations for large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computing deployment for DOE science missions. This Blueprint proposes that DOE focus on (1) deploying first-generation scientifically relevant quantum computers with at least 100 logical qubits and performing at least 10,000 to 100,000 hard logical operations in scientifically relevant calculations; (2) developing essential FTQC programming competencies, system software, and facility readiness; and (3) investing in cutting-edge focused R&D that fosters breakthroughs in scientific applications, algorithms, and logical architectures needed to accelerate the advent of scientific utility. This effort will position DOE to transition to larger systems: production-scale quantum computers that comprise 1,000 to 10,000 logical qubits, perform 1 to 10 billion hard logical operations, and execute scientifically useful computations at scale. The Blueprint calls for transformative R&D and collective action to accelerate the advent of scientific quantum utility and bring it within reach by 2028.

title: Modulations of the photoswitching performances of azobenzene-based molecular devices by the π-conjugated spacers
summary: The nature of the π-conjugated spacer is a key element to tune the electrical conductance and optical switching properties of metal-spacer-azobenzene-metal molecular devices. We report that the azobenzene-based molecular junctions with a thiophene or a phenylthiophene spacer exhibit a high cis/trans conductance ratio (ca. 1,000), while those with a bithiophene spacer have a lower conductance switching ratio (ca. 500) at the stated conditions (light wavelength and intensity) and for one batch of samples (out of two). Similarly, the two former molecular junctions have quite similar trans-to-cis isomerization kinetics, while the latter has a lower switching rate. The energy level of the highest occupied molecular orbital, which controls the electron transfer in the molecular junction, is weakly influenced by the nature of the spacer, nor by the conformation of the azobenzene moieties. The large increase in the conductance of the molecular junction with azobenzene in the cis-state is explained by an increase in the electronic coupling energy between the molecule and the top electrode. Theoretical studies by Density Functional Theory and Non Equilibrium Green's Functions are qualitatively consistent with the experiments. We find a consistent structure-property trend, showing that the higher molecule/electrode coupling energy for the cis-state is explained by the top benzene ring of the azobenzene lying flat with respect to the top electrode for the thiophene, phenylthiophene and bithiophene spacers. On the contrary, we observe that a spacer with a carbon-carbon triple bond (acetylene thiophene) induces a large irreproducibility and unpredictability of the results.

title: Lattice models of chiral random motion: A short review
summary: Chirality, a systematic rotational bias, is ubiquitous in many random motion patterns, from bacteria cells, that swim in circles near surfaces and spinning colloids, to charged particles diffusing under the influence of magnetic fields. In two dimensions, chirality renders random transport \textit{odd}: the diffusion tensor acquires an antisymmetric part that leaves the mean-squared displacement invariant but modifies fluxes and boundary currents. Lattice models for random motion are a natural setting to study chirality, since they are exactly solvable, connect directly to heterogeneous media, cellular automata, and programmable robots, and in discrete time admit fully chiral limits with a localised bulk and edge transport. Lattice walks with a rotational bias have been introduced in different communities several times since 1960, yet without a common language or conceptual connection between them. Here we review these models from the perspective that on the lattice, chirality requires memory. Taking the recently introduced chiral random walk model as a template, we describe the walker with an internal degree of freedom. With a chiral biased updating rule, the full diffusion tensor of this chiral walker turns odd. Within this picture, we can unite persistent and chiral walks, run-and-tumble motion, and cyclic random motions in one framework. We discuss how the memory is followed into the environment; in Lorentz lattice gases, kinetic and rotor walks, and random odd environments; and into the path; in spiral self-avoiding walks.

title: Curvilinear nanomagnets of non-trivial geometric topology
comment: 70 pages, 24 figures, 44y references. Chapter to appear in The Effects of Curvature in Condensed Matter Physics, eds. P. Gentile, D. Makarov, C. Ortix (Springer, Springer Tracts in Modern Physics)
summary: In this Chapter, we focus on the question of how the global geometric characteristics given by the topology of the sample's shape are reflected in the properties of the magnetization field of the given curvilinear nanoarchitecture. We start with a brief introduction to differential geometry and topology, giving their connection to the specific properties of the vector field represented by the magnetization field defined at the specific manifold. Then we discuss modern fabrication and characterization techniques that make analysis of a sample's topology not only an interesting theoretical concept but also a directly accessible and practically relevant topic. The main attention of the Chapter is dedicated to the theoretical and experimental analysis of nanostructrures with the topology different from the extended films beyond the in-depth studied topic of tubes of the constant radius. In particular, toroidal, spherical, and non-orientable manifolds are considered.

title: A macroscopic-atom spectral theory of grain-boundary segregation in multicomponent alloys
summary: Predicting grain-boundary segregation in multicomponent alloys remains challenging because existing spectral approaches require alloy-specific atomistic calculations to resolve segregation-energy distributions and correlations across non-equivalent boundary sites. Here, we develop a transferable macroscopic-atom spectral theory that predicts the joint segregation behavior of multiple species from physically interpretable elemental descriptors. The theory is founded on the finding that local strain and bond deficit account for 91\% of the site-to-site co-variation of 40 solutes in a density-functional-theory (DFT) Al polycrystal. Linked to atomic size and surface enthalpy, these coordinates allow prediction of individual segregation spectra and their cross-species correlations, which determine whether species compete for or share grain-boundary sites. A closed-system formulation unifies host-element redistribution and dilute-solute segregation, couples metallic and light-element sublattices, and accounts for bulk compound formation and solute pairing. Calibrated using binary spectra only, the theory predicts unseen-host spectral means with a correlation coefficient of 0.81, outperforms embedded-atom spectra against DFT benchmarks, and ranks site competition across 870 solute pairs with a Spearman coefficient of 0.90. Without fitting to multicomponent observations, it reproduces 11 of 12 equilibrium Fe ternaries and 49 of 55 Mg ternaries. Predictions recorded before simulations of an 82,699-atom polycrystal identify site competition as the baseline behavior and metal-metalloid pair chemistry as a source of deviations requiring atomistic resolution. These results establish a physically grounded route to screening grain-boundary chemistry in multicomponent alloys, including steels and high-entropy alloys.

title: All-electronic geometric phase gate on Doppler-cooled trapped ions using an axial mode
summary: We report the experimental demonstration of a high-fidelity oscillating magnetic gradient entangling gate on the axial stretch mode of a two-ion crystal in a micro-fabricated surface Paul trap, therefore allowing for mixed-species sympathetic cooling. With only Doppler-cooled $^{171}$Yb$^+$ ions at $\bar{n}$ = 50(5), we achieve Bell-state fidelities far above the relevant fault-tolerant threshold, simplifying transport protocols within a shuttling-based-architecture. The control fields consist only of an oscillating current applied to submerged integrated wires emitting a B-field gradient near-resonant with the axial mode, and resonant microwave pulses at the qubit frequency constituting very low gate calibration overheads. We also demonstrate an adiabatic elimination of spin-motion entanglement (AESE) version of the gate, showcasing significant robustness.

title: Electrons in a hard-wall cylinder with helicoidal metric: time-reversal pairing, cubic anticrossings, and twist-activated dipole transitions
comment: 26 pages, 17 figures, 8 tables. Corrects the analysis of E. O. Silva, Opt. Quantum Electron. 58, 113 (2026), doi:10.1007/s11082-026-08693-8, whose retraction has been requested. Scripts and verification tests are provided as ancillary files
summary: We study the scalar Schrödinger equation in a helicoidal metric when the axial direction is closed by Dirichlet walls built into the operator domain. With hard walls, the axial derivative cannot be replaced by a traveling-wave factor, and in a rotationally symmetric spinless cavity, time reversal makes the levels with azimuthal numbers $m$ and $-m$ exactly degenerate. We write the Hamiltonian as a Hermitian coupled-subband matrix and give an exact gauge-adapted variational representation. For a finite radius, the leading twist correction is quadratic, and changes sign at a critical aspect ratio; for an unbounded radial domain, it is linear in $|Ω_g|$. Retuning the aspect ratio through an isolated radial--axial resonance within one $m$ sector opens an avoided crossing with gap $Δ_{\mathrm{gap}}/E_R=1.648775\ldots|Ω_gR^2/L|^3$ to leading order. A transverse dipole transition forbidden without twist acquires an oscillator strength quadratic in the twist, with leading coefficient $0.0559408010$ for $R/L=2$ from perturbation theory. Dipole sum rules and the convergence of the currents serve as checks on the numerics. We also give the inverse-mass tensor required for a scalar realization and re-examine each statement and figure of the earlier article [Opt. Quantum Electron. \textbf{58}, 113 (2026)] within the corrected model.

title: Ordering Information in Multispecies Long-Range Swap Processes
summary: We measure how much the left-to-right species order $W_t$ of interacting particles on the integer lattice reveals about their initial configuration. For distinct species under long-range swaps, deleting stronger particles gives coordinates with independent Poisson increments. For a finitely supported initial law, the mutual information between any function $U$ of the initial configuration and $W_t$ is $C_U/t+O(t^{-3/2})$ as $t\to\infty$, where $C_U$, which may vanish, is determined by the means of Gaussian order statistics and the conditional means of the initial compressed coordinates given $U$. On consecutive sites with a uniform initial order, we compute the coefficient of the $t\log(1/t)$ term in the short-time information loss for arbitrary species counts. For three particles in this setting, repeating the weaker rather than the stronger species triples the long-time $t^{-1}$ coefficient, although both compositions have the same composition entropy and initial-order entropy. These long-time coefficients are the same whether equal particles block or push each other, but the nonuniform limiting output law is reversed. In the ordinary multispecies totally asymmetric simple exclusion process (TASEP), two distinct particles at fixed sites with a uniform initial order instead give $t^{-1/2}$ decay.

title: Contribution to the GdTe$_3$ magnetic phase diagram from electronic transport measurements
summary: Magnetic phase diagrams of the three antiferromagnetic (AFM) transitions of GdTe$_3$ that occur at zero magnetic field at $T_{N1}=12$ K, $T_{N2}=10.5$ K and $T_1=7$ K are investigated by means of resistance measurements in a magnetic field oriented along the three crystallographic directions. With the magnetic field applied in the basal plane we found re-entrance of an intermediate phase which may be a result of the coupling between the $T_{N2}$ AFM and the charge density wave with possibly a ferroaxial order. A spin flop transition is also observed at a temperature that presumably converges towards a triple point in vicinity of 2.5-3.0 T and $T$ between $T_1$ and $T_{N2}$. Our results help complete a complex phase diagram of GdTe$_3$ and advance a method for investigating magnetic ordering via transport measurements -- a technique applicable to many other compounds.

title: How Small Can a Single Shor Run Be? Limits and Constructions for secp256k1
summary: Most resource estimates for breaking secp256k1 with Shor's algorithm describe one long run per attempt, and the spacetime volume of that run, its peak number of logical qubits times its Toffoli count, sets its logical-error budget. Ekerå's tradeoff shrinks each run by using more runs, but how far it can shrink the largest run, and at what circuit cost, has not been determined. We minimize the volume of the largest run while every key is recovered with probability at least 0.99, within ten times the total volume of three runs of Häner et al.\ and $2^{40}$ classical operations. We prove that a linear run fixed in advance, which starts its group register at a point and discards its label, reveals at most $\log_2(1+(|S|-1)/r)$ bits about a uniform key, where $|S|$ counts its exponent values and $r$ is the group order. With generic post-processing and the baseline's window costs, splitting alone then shrinks the largest run at most 1.86 times within the budget. To gain more, we make each exponent bit cheaper with windows that share one table point among exponent values related by six symmetries of the curve, on a point-addition core borrowed from the ECDSA.Fail leaderboard. One random scalar and one random start per run give every approximate addition uniform operands, and a bound on each run's outcomes certifies, for every key, a decoder that discards flagged runs. We count every Toffoli gate and every qubit of every run, and each configuration solved all 563 of its pre-registered simulated trials on secp256k1. The best one shrinks the largest run 3.87 times at 8.79 times the baseline's total volume, against 2.81 times for Ekerå's tradeoff on the same core, and its run is at least 2.6 times smaller than every design of Initio Intelligence.

title: Intrinsic longitudinal Hall effect in ferroaxial metals with high-order rotation axes
summary: The low-field Hall resistivity of non-magnetic metals has an intrinsic quantum contribution that derives from the field-corrected Berry curvature and intrinsic magnetic moment of the Bloch states near the Fermi surface. However, its effect is usually overshadowed by the classical Lorentz-force contribution. Here we show that for the longitudinal Hall effect, which occurs in ferroaxial crystals when the applied magnetic field lies in the Hall plane, the Lorentz force contribution vanishes for the eight ferroaxial groups with a 3,4 or 6-fold rotation axis. This provides an opportunity to measure the quantum correction in isolation, but so far all measured instances of the effect fall in the remaining five ferroaxial groups of lower symmetry, where the Lorentz force dominates the signal. We compile a list of candidate ferroaxial metals with such high-order rotation axis and compute the Hall effect from first principles for representative candidates, identifying Ni$_3$P with $σ^{\rm H}_{xzx} = 28.4$ S/m/T as a promising material to unambiguously measure the intrinsic longitudinal Hall effect.

title: Entanglement Asymmetry and the Quantum Mpemba Effect in Inhomogeneous Quenches
summary: Entanglement asymmetry is a powerful probe of symmetry breaking and its dynamical restoration following quantum quenches. While extensively studied for homogeneous initial states, its evolution from inhomogeneous initial configurations remains largely unexplored. We investigate a spin-$1/2$ XX chain whose two halves are initially prepared in tilted ferromagnetic states with different tilt angles. Combining generalized hydrodynamics (GHD) and the quasiparticle picture with exact fermionic correlation-matrix calculations, we study the dynamics of entanglement asymmetry. We find good agreement between the two approaches for generic initial configurations and observe the quantum Mpemba effect, whereby states with stronger initial symmetry breaking can restore the symmetry faster. This effect now depends on the subsystem position: while the homogeneous behavior is recovered when the subsystem lies entirely within one of the initially tilted halves, the entanglement-asymmetry curves for subsystems straddling the interface can exhibit multiple crossings or no crossings at all. A notable exception occurs for subsystems entirely within an initially non-tilted half. In this case, GHD predicts vanishing asymmetry, but the exact dynamics generates a small, nonzero asymmetry that can develop a plateau before decaying toward zero. This feature reveals contributions beyond the leading-order hydrodynamic description.

title: Mixing and Preserving Properties of Non-van der Waals 2D Materials in Sandwich-like Heterostructures
summary: Heterostructure interfaces created by stacking two-dimensional (2D) materials outline an appealing route towards achieving advanced electronic and magnetic functionalities at the nanoscale. Non-van der Waals (non-vdW) sandwich-like heterostructures (HSs) are build out of non-vdW 2D materials derived from non-layered crystals and establish a new frontier enabling strong interfacial coupling. Employing ab initio density functional theory (DFT), we investigate two classes of such trilayer HSs: purely non-vdW assemblies and hybrid vdW/non-vdW/vdW stacks. We show that non-vdW sandwiches undergo pronounced geometric reconstruction forming chemically bonded interfaces with large absolute binding energies up to an order of magnitude larger than those of conventional vdW HSs. These strong interactions drive extensive electronic hybridization, band gap renormalization, and tunable interlayer magnetic coupling. In contrast, vdW encapsulation largely protects the intrinsic atomic and electronic structure of the non-vdW sheet from the environment , while enabling charge transfer doping of the vdW layers. Our results thus establish sandwich HSs a versatile interface design platform, spanning interaction regimes from weakly perturbed encapsulation to strongly interacting chemically bonded systems with emergent electronic and magnetic behavior.

title: Entanglement between distant spins in a polarized magnet forms a $d$-wave clover
comment: 8 pages, 4 figures, including End Matter; Supplemental Material (99 pages, 2 figures) appended. Code and data in the ancillary files
summary: Spin-orbit coupling makes a polarized magnet a source of virtual spin-flip pairs. These pairs entangle distant spins: the symmetry of the coupling fixes the angular pattern, and the flips they leave behind end it at a distance of order the inverse spin-orbit angle. For a spin-1/2 square-lattice ferromagnet we prove, at leading order, a d-wave inverse-square law, 1.376 times the spin-wave amplitude, a clover-shaped entangled region, exact without the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya term, and that each spin's entanglement is entirely pairwise. Four qubits can test the d-wave signs at present error rates.

title: Neural Decoding of Logical Clifford Circuits with Transversal Gates
comment: 28 pages, 4 figures, 21 tables. Code, trained networks and raw data: https://github.com/a85tract/Duet
summary: On neutral-atom and trapped-ion machines, a transversal gate needs only one syndrome round, so a logical gate takes up to d times less time than with lattice surgery. However, transversal gates make decoding harder, because a transversal CNOT copies errors between two blocks of physical qubits, so a decoder must read all blocks of a circuit together. Algorithmic decoders for such circuits gain accuracy at the cost of speed. Neural decoders ease this trade-off, but they must infer from data where errors go across each gate and how logical outcomes propagate through the circuit, although both are known exactly. In this work, we present Duet, a neural decoder for logical Clifford circuits with transversal gates that builds in this known information and learns only which errors occurred. Duet leverages three insights. First, each transversal gate moves an error to a fixed place, so the network exchanges features only between the sites that a gate connects. Second, a logical outcome propagates through Clifford gates exactly and linearly, so the network predicts only the flips that the errors of each layer cause and combines the layers by a soft XOR. Third, every circuit is built from the same few gates, so the network takes the gates of each layer as input and one network per code distance decodes circuits of different sizes and depths. We pair Duet with the search decoder Tesseract, which re-decodes the few shots on which the network is least confident. On general circuits with 2 to 4 blocks and up to 16 layers, Duet alone is already more accurate than matching at every distance, and with Tesseract it fails 44 times less often than LoMatching at distance 9. On the random circuits of the Lukin group, it fails 0.299 times as often as their neural decoder at distance 7. The composition stays fast and takes 2.4 to 121.7 μs per layer, less than their network takes per gate at every distance.

title: Recovery of Extended Modes from the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect Due to Local Nonlinearity on a Boundary
summary: Localization in continuum spectra known as the non-Hermitian skin effect is widely believed to be a consequence of nontrivial topology of bulk bands. However, the robustness of the non-Hermitian skin effect against nonlinear effects is still a nontrivial problem. We here reveal that single-bond nonlinearity on a boundary can recover extended modes in a non-Hermitian tight-binding model. We propose and analyze a one-dimensional minimal model, where we introduce a nonlinear phase shift of a hopping term only at boundary sites. We also propose a possible photonic setup to dynamically observe the nonlinearity-induced extended modes as a steady state. Our results thus challenge the conventional notion of the non-Hermitian skin effect by revealing its dependence on nonlinear boundary conditions.

title: Anomalous front propagation in many-body quantum transport with memory-dependent resetting
summary: We introduce an exactly solvable framework for non-Markovian quantum many-body dynamics based on stochastic resetting with memory. Applicable to arbitrary time-independent Hamiltonians, including interacting systems, our framework provides an exact representation of the dynamics with memory in terms of the corresponding reset-free evolution, which can be accessed either analytically or numerically. We demonstrate the power of this approach by studying domain-wall melting in a one-dimensional chain of noninteracting fermions, obtaining exact analytical results for the density profile, the local structure of the front edge, the extreme-value statistics of the rightmost fermion, and the integrated current. Remarkably, memory transforms ballistic transport into logarithmically slow propagation without arresting spreading. While the macroscopic density profile retains its original scaling function, the front edge broadens as $\sqrt{\ln t}$ rather than $t^{1/3}$ at late times and develops a qualitatively different edge structure. Furthermore, the extreme-value statistics change from Tracy--Widom to Gaussian, while both the mean and variance of the integrated current grow logarithmically in time. Our predictions are in excellent agreement with numerical simulations. These results reveal how memory can fundamentally alter quantum many-body transport and its fluctuations.

title: Zone-folded Goldstone mode of the field-induced spin supersolid in the square-lattice $S=1$ antiferromagnet
summary: The field-induced spin supersolid of the square-lattice $S=1$ antiferromagnet with single-ion and exchange anisotropy has so far been characterized only by static observables, among them a two-peak transverse structure factor. We compute its dynamic spin structure factors, and those of the neighboring phases, by stochastic analytic continuation of stochastic-series-expansion quantum Monte Carlo data on a $16\times16$ lattice at inverse temperature $β=32$, at one field in each of the supersolid, the $m_z=1/2$ Ising plateau and the canted $XY$ phase. The supersolid has a single Goldstone mode, which the checkerboard folds onto both the ordering wave vector $\mathbf{Q}=(π,π)$ and $\mathbf{q}=(0,0)$, so that it appears in both spin channels at both points with one velocity $v=1.36\pm0.01$. The canted phase shows half of this pattern and the plateau none, the latter carrying instead a gapped magnon band and a two-magnon longitudinal continuum. Exactly at $\mathbf{Q}$ and $(0,0)$ the finite-lattice spectra are governed by a rotor tower of the condensate in the transverse channel and an Ising doublet of the checkerboard in the longitudinal one, both present at $\mathbf{Q}$ in the supersolid. Three parameter-free comparisons with the stiffness and the uniform susceptibility of the same runs, for the velocity, the sound-mode weight and the thermal decay of the rotor tower, tie the continued spectra to raw Monte Carlo observables. The folded Goldstone mode is the dynamical fingerprint of the supersolid.

title: Neutron Spectroscopy Transformed: Deuterated ZIF-8 and Machine-Learned Potentials Catch Nitrogen Threading Its Gates
comment: 34 pages, 5 figures; Supporting Information (19 figures) included; Movie S1 as an ancillary file
summary: We report a step change in what inelastic neutron scattering (INS) can reveal, by combining machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) with deliberate deuteration of the sample. INS's prowess in charting framework and guest motions within porous materials during in situ dosing has historically had one caveat: costly density-functional-theory calculations are a major bottleneck in the speed and depth of analysis. We show that rapid frontier MLIPs remove this bottleneck on both counts, keeping pace with the experiment while bringing a new level of insight. Deuterating the linkers of ZIF-8 pries apart bands that overlap in the hydrogenous framework, and we test four MLIPs against eight stages of nitrogen dosing at 77 K. On loading, a previously unobserved band appears at 270 cm^-1 and grows gradually through the dosing series. The simulations trace it to single N2 molecules threaded end-on through four-ring windows, each turning its ring of linkers and propping the window open, and unbiased dynamics catch molecules threading into the windows on their own, finding a free-energy trap that crowding stabilizes. This is the first vibrational signature of the threaded state and, crucially, its intensity directly counts the threading over the slow, macroscopic timescale of gas uptake, in situ. More broadly, the simulations explain how each framework band responds to its guests, establishing MLIP-assisted inelastic neutron scattering as a route to mechanism, not just assignment.

title: The role of composition rules in an axiomatic derivation of quantum mechanics
summary: Local discriminability and purification are two key axioms in an information-theoretic axiomatization of quantum mechanics as proposed by G. M. D'Ariano et al. (Quantum Theory from First Principles, 2017). Both of them refer to compound systems, the theory of which is rather directly assumed to be given by the tensor product structure. This structure, though well understood, should, however, be based on a more careful study of formal composition rules describing how local effects can be embedded into the compound effect space and how to reduce joint states onto subsystems. In that we follow the earlier work of T. Matolcsi, (Acta Sci. Math., 1975), and D. Aerts and I. Daubechies, (Helvetica Physica Acta, 1978), as summarized, e.g., in The Logic of Quantum Mechanics, 1981, by E. Beltrametti and G. Cassinelli. We also establish axioms of local discrimination stating that compound states can be told apart by local measurements the notion of which we also formally define. The purification axioms first introduced as axioms of quantum mechanics by D'Ariano et al. are also rewritten in a weaker form which we believe could be fruitful for future axiomatizations. These reformulations bring us closer to proper tensor product structures for joint state and effect spaces, so that the embedding map for states factors through the projective tensor product of the local state spaces and the embedding map for effects factors through the injective tensor product of the local effect spaces. We also discuss the case of multipartite composition axioms and associativity properties required in these settings.

title: Scaling Limits of Time-averaged Distributions for Symmetric Quantum Walks on Hypercubes
summary: We study continuous-time and discrete-time quantum walks on the hypercube $\{0,1\}^d$ associated with symmetric random walks, that is, random walks whose transition probabilities depend only on the Hamming distance, using the Hamming scheme and Krawtchouk polynomials. For continuous-time walks, we show that the time-averaged distribution of the Hamming distance is a discrete arcsine law whenever the eigenvalues are distinct. For discrete-time walks, exact formulas for the time-averaged distribution are known as combinatorial sums or as mixtures involving Krawtchouk polynomials, but their scaling limits as $d\to\infty$ (time average first) have not been specified. We obtain them explicitly for three random walks: the simple random walk (an arcsine law), the random walk with binomial weights (an equal mixture of arcsine laws with different supports), and the independent random walk (atoms of mass $1/2$ at $0$ and at $1/2$). Comparing with the continuous-time limits, the two models agree for the simple random walk but differ for the other two, so the correspondence between them is not universal.

title: Classification of spin space groups and crystal magnetic orders
summary: Spin space groups (SSGs) describe magnetic crystals in the limit of negligible spin-orbit coupling, where spatial and spin rotations decouple. Although algebraic enumerations of SSGs exist, their abstract mathematical approaches obscure the physical meaning of the resulting classifications, leaving the direct correspondence between SSGs and real-space magnetic orders unestablished. Here, we present a physically motivated framework for enumerating and classifying SSGs based on their translation holonomy---the image of the spatial lattice translation group under the spin homomorphism. The three classes of abelian images in $SO(3)$ divide SSGs into three basic translation types. Translation holonomy constrains the spin operations associated with point-group elements, yielding a complete enumeration of SSGs organized by a physical hierarchy. Within this framework, translation holonomy classifies SSGs and magnetic orders into 17 universal spin-lattice types, each with unambiguous Bragg-peak geometries and polarization signatures in neutron diffraction. Beyond organizing known magnetic orders, this framework directly predicts four universal physical phenomena: (i) exact magnetization compensation enforced by certain spin-lattice types; (ii) an exact group-theoretic criterion for the emergence of noncommuting Brillouin zones; (iii) a new type of 3Q magnetic order with vanishing octupoles; and (iv) the realization of strictly collinear momentum-space spin textures protected by reflection-staggered coplanar spin lattices. We also construct a spin space group database organized according to this physical hierarchy.

title: Energy transport from an active medium
summary: We study the energy current through a harmonic chain whose left end is coupled, via a short-range contact potential, to a medium of overdamped run-and-tumble particles moving on a ring, while the right end is attached to a zero-temperature Langevin reservoir. The activity is parametrized by the propulsion speed $v_0$ and the persistence time $τ$. Using nonequilibrium response theory at weak system-medium coupling, we predict the stationary current and simulations reproduce it over a large part of the $(v_0,τ)$ plane. That includes the possible nonmonotonicity of the current as function of $v_0$ and $τ$, and occurrence of resonances with the normal modes of the chain, most significantly at large $τ$ and small $v_0$. There is a critical propulsion speed $v_c$ at which the ring-crossing frequency of the particles leaves the phonon band: for $v_0<v_c$ the current grows with persistence, while for $v_0>v_c$ it decays as $(v_0^2τ)^{-1}$. We also explain where the theoretical prediction fails, especially due to an oscillatory instability originating from a sufficiently strong negative friction induced on the leftmost oscillator. Finally, the persistent medium produces strongly non-Gaussian velocity statistics and long-range, oscillating velocity correlations in the bulk of the chain.

title: Local Thermodynamic Reconstruction of Impurity Entropy
summary: Resolving the thermodynamic entropy associated with a local impurity in a spatially extended interacting quantum bath remains a numerical challenge. We develop a Local-Maxwell approach that reconstructs the impurity entropy from local observables in worldline quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations. By integrating their temperature responses along the impurity coupling, the method avoids separate estimates of extensive entropies. For nonnegative worldline expansions with bounded local couplings, we establish bath-size independent bounds on all factorial moments of the impurity vertex count. For even vertex counts, the Maxwell estimator variance remains bounded as the coupling approaches zero. The transverse-field Ising benchmark reproduces exact free fermion results, while an interacting XXZ chain demonstrates up to several hundredfold improvement in statistical efficiency over conventional extensive thermodynamic integration. In a three-channel XXZ impurity junction, we reveal entropy recovery upon cooling and a nonmonotonic coupling dependence of the finite-temperature entropy contrast. These results establish local thermodynamic reconstruction as an efficient approach to impurity entropy in interacting quantum baths.

title: Lattice Thermal Conductivity of MgO and the MgSiO$_3$ Polymorphs Bridgmanite and Post-Perovskite at Lower-Mantle Conditions Using Fine-Tuned MACE Potentials
summary: Heat flow across the core-mantle boundary (CMB) depends on the lattice thermal conductivity ($κ_{\mathrm{latt}}$) of lowermost-mantle minerals, yet calculated CMB values for MgO differ severalfold, and high-temperature estimates of the conductivity increase across the bridgmanite-post-perovskite transition range from about 20 to 50%. Direct solutions of the linearized phonon Boltzmann transport equation (LBTE) require thousands of density functional theory (DFT) force evaluations per thermodynamic state. Here we replace these evaluations with phase-specific, fine-tuned MACE potentials for MgO, MgSiO3 bridgmanite (Pv), and MgSiO3 post-perovskite (PPv). The potentials reproduce DFT energies, forces, stresses, pressure-volume relations, and compressed-state phonons for all three phases. For MgO at 0 GPa, replacing MACE forces with DFT forces in otherwise identical transport calculations changes $κ_{\mathrm{latt}}$ by 0.2% at 300 K and 1.9% at 2000 K. PPv is 44-55% more conductive than Pv at the same pressure and temperature and strongly anisotropic, with $κ_{[100]}/κ_{[010]}$ ranging from 1.7 to 2.1. The quasi-harmonic phase boundary has a Clapeyron slope of $(7.4 \pm 0.1)$ MPa/K and intersects a model geotherm at 116.2 GPa and 2660 K, where the transition raises the silicate conductivity by 47%, to 8.6 W/(m K). Heating in the basal thermal boundary layer lowers the MgO and PPv conductivities to 37.3 and 6.7 W/(m K) at the CMB, where Hashin-Shtrikman bounds of 9.5-11.4 W/(m K) for an Fe-free aggregate of 80 vol% silicate and 20 vol% MgO encompass the 10 W/(m K) used in earlier heat-flow estimates. The density-temperature parameterizations provide an intrinsic end-member reference for lower-mantle thermal models.

title: Topological insulators on site-eliminated, projected, and patterned fractal lattices
summary: Identifying fractal lattices of fractional (Hausdorff) dimension as geometric descendants of parent crystals, we showcase the successful realization of canonical topological insulators in one-, two-, and three-dimensional crystals on their self-similar descents using three complementary approaches, starting from lattice-regularized models in integer dimensions. (a) In the first approach, we construct the fractal Hamiltonian by removing all parent-lattice sites that do not belong to such a network (method of site elimination). (b) In the second one, we integrate or project out the same set of sites to obtain an effective Hamiltonian for the fractal lattice (method of projection or renormalization). (c) In the third approach, we retain the parent-crystal lattice intact but spatially pattern the on-site mass parameter, which controls the topology of the parent insulating system, such that it assumes two topologically distinct values on the fractal network and its complement (patterned fractal lattices). By numerically diagonalizing the resulting Hamiltonians and computing appropriate topological invariants or local markers, corroborating the bulk-boundary correspondence through gapless modes at outer or inner boundaries, we establish Su-Schrieffer-Heeger topology on the Cantor set using all three approaches, Haldane topology on the hexaflake [using (a) and (b)] and Qi-Wu-Zhang topology on the Sierpiński carpet [using (c)], and strong $Z_2$ topological insulating phases on the tiled Menger sponge from methods (a), (b), and (c). These findings complement and substantially extend the previously reported realization of Qi-Wu-Zhang topology on the Sierpiński carpet using methods (a) and (b) [Phys. Rev. B 110, L241302 (2024)].

title: Systematic and accurate anharmonic formation free energies of metastable defects via a constrained Bayesian Adaptive Biasing Force framework
summary: Computing the formation free energies of metastable defects at finite temperature remains challenging due to anharmonicity, the multiplicity of basins and the frequent occurrence of migration events. Using the previously introduced constrained Bayesian Adaptive Biasing Force method (BABFc), we establish a practical thermodynamic integration framework for computing restricted anharmonic formation free energies associated with individual metastable defect basins. We demonstrate that BABFc can be exploited as a robust, systematic and numerically efficient tool for addressing a long standing bottleneck in atomistic materials science: the finite temperature thermodynamic characterization of metastable defects in complex, highly anharmonic energy landscapes. The proposed workflow requires only a reference local minimum and a confinement strategy and does not rely on defect specific collective variables. It therefore provides a general route to assign well-defined free energies to individual metastable basins, even when these basins are separated by low barriers and embedded in a dense landscape of competing configurations.
